Introduction\\\\nProgress in speech recognition has been energized by the\\\\ndevelopment of unsupervised pre-training techniques exem-\\\\npliﬁed by Wav2Vec 2.0 (Baevski et al., 2020). Since these\\\\nmethods learn directly from raw audio without the need for\\\\nhuman labels, they can productively use large datasets of un-\\\\nlabeled speech and have been quickly scaled up to 1,000,000\\\\nhours of training data (Zhang et al., 2021), far more than the\\\\n1,000 or so hours typical of an academic supervised dataset.\\\\nWhen ﬁne-tuned on standard benchmarks, this approach\\\\nhas improved the state of the art, especially in a low-data\\\\nsetting.\\\\nThese pre-trained audio encoders learn high-quality repre-\\\\nsentations of speech, but because they are purely unsuper-\\\\nvised they lack an equivalently performant decoder mapping\\\\nthose representations to usable outputs, necessitating a ﬁne-\\\\ntuning stage in order to actually perform a task such as\\\\nspeech recognition1. This unfortunately limits their use-\\\\nfulness and impact as ﬁne-tuning can still be a complex\\\\nprocess requiring a skilled practitioner. There is an addi-\\\\ntional risk with requiring ﬁne-tuning. Machine learning\\\\n*Equal contribution 1OpenAI, San Francisco, CA 94110, USA.\\\\nCorrespondence to: Alec Radford <alec@openai.com>, Jong\\\\nWook Kim <jongwook@openai.com>.\\\\n1Baevski et al. (2021) is an exciting exception - having devel-\\\\noped a fully unsupervised speech recognition system\\\\nmethods are exceedingly adept at ﬁnding patterns within a\\\\ntraining dataset which boost performance on held-out data\\\\nfrom the same dataset. However, some of these patterns are\\\\nbrittle and spurious and don’t generalize to other datasets\\\\nand distributions. In a particularly disturbing example, Rad-\\\\nford et al. (2021) documented a 9.2% increase in object\\\\nclassiﬁcation accuracy when ﬁne-tuning a computer vision\\\\nmodel on the ImageNet dataset (Russakovsky et al., 2015)\\\\nwithout observing any improvement in average accuracy\\\\nwhen classifying the same objects on seven other natural\\\\nimage datasets. A model that achieves “superhuman” per-\\\\nformance when trained on a dataset can still make many\\\\nbasic errors when evaluated on another, possibly precisely\\\\nbecause it is exploiting those dataset-speciﬁc quirks that\\\\nhumans are oblivious to (Geirhos et al., 2020).\\\\nThis suggests that while unsupervised pre-training has im-\\\\nproved the quality of audio encoders dramatically, the lack\\\\nof an equivalently high-quality pre-trained decoder, com-\\\\nbined with a recommended protocol of dataset-speciﬁc ﬁne-\\\\ntuning, is a crucial weakness which limits their usefulness\\\\nand robustness. The goal of a speech recognition system\\\\nshould be to work reliably “out of the box” in a broad range\\\\nof environments without requiring supervised ﬁne-tuning of\\\\na decoder for every deployment distribution.\\\\nAs demonstrated by Narayanan et al. (2018), Likhomanenko\\\\net al. (2020), and Chan et al. (2021) speech recognition sys-\\\\ntems that are pre-trained in a supervised fashion across many\\\\ndatasets/domains exhibit higher robustness and generalize\\\\nmuch more effectively to held-out datasets than models\\\\ntrained on a single source. These works achieve this by\\\\ncombining as many existing high-quality speech recogni-\\\\ntion datasets as possible. However, there is still only a\\\\nmoderate amount of this data easily available. SpeechStew\\\\n(Chan et al., 2021) mixes together 7 pre-existing datasets\\\\ntotalling 5,140 hours of supervision. While not insigniﬁ-\\\\ncant, this is still tiny compared to the previously mentioned\\\\n1,000,000 hours of unlabeled speech data utilized in Zhang\\\\net al. (2021).\\\\nRecognizing the limiting size of existing high-quality super-\\\\nvised datasets, recent efforts have created larger datasets for\\\\nspeech recognition. By relaxing the requirement of gold-\\\\nstandard human-validated transcripts, Chen et al. (2021) and\\\\nGalvez et al. (2021) make use of sophisticated automated\\\\narXiv:2212.04356v1  [eess.AS]  6 Dec 2022\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 2 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n2\\\\npipelines to scale weakly supervised speech recognition\\\\nto 10,000 and 30,000 hours of noisier training data. This\\\\ntrade-off between quality and quantity is often the right\\\\ncall. Although understudied so far for speech recognition,\\\\nrecent work in computer vision has demonstrated that mov-\\\\ning beyond gold-standard crowdsourced datasets such as\\\\nImageNet (Russakovsky et al., 2015) to much larger but\\\\nweakly supervised datasets signiﬁcantly improves the ro-\\\\nbustness and generalization of models (Mahajan et al., 2018;\\\\nKolesnikov et al., 2020).\\\\nYet these new datasets are only a few times larger than the\\\\nsum of existing high-quality datasets and still much smaller\\\\nthan prior unsupervised work. In this work we close that\\\\ngap, scaling weakly supervised speech recognition the next\\\\norder of magnitude to 680,000 hours of labeled audio data.\\\\nWe call our approach Whisper2. We demonstrate models\\\\ntrained at this scale transfer well to existing datasets zero-\\\\nshot, removing the need for any dataset-speciﬁc ﬁne-tuning\\\\nto achieve high-quality results.\\\\nIn addition to scale, our work also focuses on broaden-\\\\ning the scope of weakly supervised pre-training beyond\\\\nEnglish-only speech recognition to be both multilingual and\\\\nmultitask. Of those 680,000 hours of audio, 117,000 hours\\\\ncover 96 other languages. The dataset also includes 125,000\\\\nhours of X→en translation data. We ﬁnd that for sufﬁciently\\\\nlarge models there is no drawback and even beneﬁts to joint\\\\nmultilingual and multitask training.\\\\nOur work suggests that simple scaling of weakly supervised\\\\npre-training has been underappreciated so far for speech\\\\nrecognition. We achieve these results without the need for\\\\nthe self-supervision or self-training techniques that have\\\\nbeen a mainstay of recent large-scale speech recognition\\\\nwork. To serve as a foundation for further research on robust\\\\nspeech recognition, we release inference code and models at\\\\nthe following URL: https://github.com/openai/\\\\nwhisper.\\\\n2. Approach\\\\n2.1. Data Processing\\\\nFollowing the trend of recent work leveraging web-scale\\\\ntext from the internet for training machine learning systems,\\\\nwe take a minimalist approach to data pre-processing. In\\\\ncontrast to a lot of work on speech recognition, we train\\\\nWhisper models to predict the raw text of transcripts without\\\\nany signiﬁcant standardization, relying on the expressive-\\\\nness of sequence-to-sequence models to learn to map be-\\\\ntween utterances and their transcribed form. This simpliﬁes\\\\n2If an acronym or basis for the name is desired, WSPSR stand-\\\\ning for Web-scale Supervised Pretraining for Speech Recognition\\\\ncan be used.\\\\nthe speech recognition pipeline since it removes the need\\\\nfor a separate inverse text normalization step in order to\\\\nproduce naturalistic transcriptions.\\\\nWe construct the dataset from audio that is paired with tran-\\\\nscripts on the Internet. This results in a very diverse dataset\\\\ncovering a broad distribution of audio from many different\\\\nenvironments, recording setups, speakers, and languages.\\\\nWhile diversity in audio quality can help train a model to be\\\\nrobust, diversity in transcript quality is not similarly bene-\\\\nﬁcial. Initial inspection showed a large amount of subpar\\\\ntranscripts in the raw dataset. To address this, we developed\\\\nseveral automated ﬁltering methods to improve transcript\\\\nquality.\\\\nMany transcripts on the internet are not actually human-\\\\ngenerated but the output of existing ASR systems. Recent\\\\nresearch has shown that training on datasets of mixed human\\\\nand machine-generated data can signiﬁcantly impair the per-\\\\nformance of translation systems (Ghorbani et al., 2021). In\\\\norder to avoid learning “transcript-ese”, we developed many\\\\nheuristics to detect and remove machine-generated tran-\\\\nscripts from the training dataset. Many existing ASR sys-\\\\ntems output only a limited subset of written language which\\\\nremoves or normalizes away aspects that are difﬁcult to pre-\\\\ndict from only audio signals such as complex punctuation\\\\n(exclamation points, commas, and question marks), format-\\\\nting whitespace such as paragraphs, or stylistic aspects such\\\\nas capitalization. An all-uppercase or all-lowercase tran-\\\\nscript is very unlikely to be human generated. While many\\\\nASR systems include some level of inverse text normaliza-\\\\ntion, it is often simple or rule-based and still detectable from\\\\nother unhandled aspects such as never including commas.\\\\nWe also use an audio language detector, which was created\\\\nby ﬁne-tuning a prototype model trained on a prototype ver-\\\\nsion of the dataset on VoxLingua107 (Valk & Alum¨ae, 2021)\\\\nto ensure that the spoken language matches the language of\\\\nthe transcript according to CLD2. If the two do not match,\\\\nwe don’t include the (audio, transcript) pair as a speech\\\\nrecognition training example in the dataset. We make an\\\\nexception if the transcript language is English and add these\\\\npairs to the dataset as X→en speech translation training\\\\nexamples instead. We use fuzzy de-duping of transcript\\\\ntexts to reduce the amount of duplication and automatically\\\\ngenerated content in the training dataset.\\\\nWe break audio ﬁles into 30-second segments paired with\\\\nthe subset of the transcript that occurs within that time\\\\nsegment. We train on all audio, including segments where\\\\nthere is no speech (though with sub-sampled probability)\\\\nand use these segments as training data for voice activity\\\\ndetection.\\\\nFor an additional ﬁltering pass, after training an initial model\\\\nwe aggregated information about its error rate on training\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 3 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n3\\\\ndata sources and performed manual inspection of these data\\\\nsources sorting by a combination of both high error rate and\\\\ndata source size in order to identify and remove low-quality\\\\nones efﬁciently. This inspection showed a large amount of\\\\nonly partially transcribed or poorly aligned/misaligned tran-\\\\nscripts as well as remaining low-quality machine-generated\\\\ncaptions that ﬁltering heuristics did not detect.\\\\nTo avoid contamination, we perform de-duplication at a tran-\\\\nscript level between the training dataset and the evaluation\\\\ndatasets we thought were at higher risk of overlap, namely\\\\nTED-LIUM 3 (Hernandez et al., 2018).\\\\n2.2. Model\\\\nSince the focus of our work is on studying the capabilities\\\\nof large-scale supervised pre-training for speech recogni-\\\\ntion, we use an off-the-shelf architecture to avoid confound-\\\\ning our ﬁndings with model improvements. We chose an\\\\nencoder-decoder Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) as this\\\\narchitecture has been well validated to scale reliably. All\\\\naudio is re-sampled to 16,000 Hz, and an 80-channel log-\\\\nmagnitude Mel spectrogram representation is computed on\\\\n25-millisecond windows with a stride of 10 milliseconds.\\\\nFor feature normalization, we globally scale the input to\\\\nbe between -1 and 1 with approximately zero mean across\\\\nthe pre-training dataset. The encoder processes this input\\\\nrepresentation with a small stem consisting of two convolu-\\\\ntion layers with a ﬁlter width of 3 and the GELU activation\\\\nfunction (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) where the second\\\\nconvolution layer has a stride of two. Sinusoidal position\\\\nembeddings are then added to the output of the stem after\\\\nwhich the encoder Transformer blocks are applied. The\\\\ntransformer uses pre-activation residual blocks (Child et al.,\\\\n2019), and a ﬁnal layer normalization is applied to the en-\\\\ncoder output. The decoder uses learned position embeddings\\\\nand tied input-output token representations (Press & Wolf,\\\\n2017). The encoder and decoder have the same width and\\\\nnumber of transformer blocks. Figure 1 summarizes the\\\\nmodel architecture.\\\\nWe use the same byte-level BPE text tokenizer used in GPT-\\\\n2 (Sennrich et al., 2015; Radford et al., 2019) for the English-\\\\nonly models and reﬁt the vocabulary (but keep the same size)\\\\nfor the multilingual models to avoid excessive fragmenta-\\\\ntion on other languages since the GPT-2 BPE vocabulary is\\\\nEnglish only.\\\\n2.3. Multitask Format\\\\nAlthough predicting which words were spoken in a given\\\\naudio snippet is a core part of the full speech recognition\\\\nproblem and extensively studied in research, it is not the\\\\nonly part. A fully featured speech recognition system can\\\\ninvolve many additional components such as voice activ-\\\\nity detection, speaker diarization, and inverse text normal-\\\\nization. These components are often handled separately,\\\\nresulting in a relatively complex system around the core\\\\nspeech recognition model. To reduce this complexity, we\\\\nwould like to have a single model perform the entire speech\\\\nprocessing pipeline, not just the core recognition part. An\\\\nimportant consideration here is the interface for the model.\\\\nThere are many different tasks that can be performed on\\\\nthe same input audio signal: transcription, translation, voice\\\\nactivity detection, alignment, and language identiﬁcation\\\\nare some examples.\\\\nFor this kind of one-to-many mapping to work with a single\\\\nmodel, some form of task speciﬁcation is necessary. We use\\\\na simple format to specify all tasks and conditioning infor-\\\\nmation as a sequence of input tokens to the decoder. Since\\\\nour decoder is an audio-conditional language model, we also\\\\ntrain it to condition on the history of text of the transcript in\\\\nthe hope that it will learn to use longer-range text context\\\\nto resolve ambiguous audio. Speciﬁcally, with some proba-\\\\nbility we add the transcript text preceding the current audio\\\\nsegment to the decoder’s context. We indicate the beginning\\\\nof prediction with a <|startoftranscript|> token.\\\\nFirst, we predict the language being spoken which is repre-\\\\nsented by a unique token for each language in our training\\\\nset (99 total). These language targets are sourced from the\\\\naforementioned VoxLingua107 model. In the case where\\\\nthere is no speech in an audio segment, the model is trained\\\\nto predict a <|nospeech|> token indicating this. The\\\\nnext token speciﬁes the task (either transcription or trans-\\\\nlation) with an <|transcribe|> or <|translate|>\\\\ntoken. After this, we specify whether to predict timestamps\\\\nor not by including a <|notimestamps|> token for that\\\\ncase. At this point, the task and desired format is fully\\\\nspeciﬁed, and the output begins. For timestamp predic-\\\\ntion, we predict time relative to the current audio segment,\\\\nquantizing all times to the nearest 20 milliseconds which\\\\nmatches the native time resolution of Whisper models, and\\\\nadd additional tokens to our vocabulary for each of these.\\\\nWe interleave their prediction with the caption tokens: the\\\\nstart time token is predicted before each caption’s text, and\\\\nthe end time token is predicted after. When a ﬁnal tran-\\\\nscript segment is only partially included in the current 30-\\\\nsecond audio chunk, we predict only its start time token\\\\nfor the segment when in timestamp mode, to indicate that\\\\nthe subsequent decoding should be performed on an au-\\\\ndio window aligned with that time, otherwise we truncate\\\\nthe audio to not include the segment. Lastly, we add a\\\\n<|endoftranscript|> token. We only mask out the\\\\ntraining loss over the previous context text, and train the\\\\nmodel to predict all other tokens. Please see Figure 1 for an\\\\noverview of our format and training setup.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 4 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n4\\\\n⋯\\\\n⋯\\\\n2 × Conv1D + GELU\\\\n⋮\\\\ncross attention\\\\nLog-Mel Spectrogram\\\\n~\\\\nSOT\\\\nEN\\\\nTRANS-\\\\nCRIBE\\\\n0.0\\\\nThe quick\\\\nTokens in Multitask Training Format\\\\nTransformer\\\\nEncoder Blocks\\\\nTransformer\\\\nDecoder Blocks\\\\nEN\\\\n0.0\\\\nThe quick brown\\\\n⋮\\\\n⋮\\\\nnext-token\\\\nprediction\\\\nSinusoidal\\\\nPositional\\\\nEncoding\\\\nLearned\\\\nPositional\\\\nEncoding\\\\nMultitask training data (680k hours)\\\\nSequence-to-sequence learning\\\\nMultitask training format\\\\nEnglish transcription\\\\nAny-to-English speech translation\\\\nNon-English transcription\\\\nNo speech\\\\n🗣️  “Ask not what your country can do for ⋯”\\\\n📝  Ask not what your country can do for ⋯\\\\n🗣️  “El rápido zorro marrón salta sobre ⋯”\\\\n📝  The quick brown fox jumps over ⋯\\\\n🗣️ “언덕 위에 올라 내려다보면 너무나 넓고 넓은 ⋯”\\\\n📝  언덕 위에 올라 내려다보면 너무나 넓고 넓은 ⋯\\\\n🔊 (background music playing)\\\\n📝  ∅\\\\nPREV\\\\nspecial\\\\ntokens\\\\ntext\\\\ntokens\\\\ntimestamp\\\\ntokens\\\\nSTART OF\\\\nTRANSCRIPT\\\\nLANGUAGE\\\\nTAG\\\\nNO\\\\nSPEECH\\\\nEOT\\\\nTRANSCRIBE\\\\nTRANSLATE\\\\nbegin\\\\ntime\\\\nNO\\\\nTIMESTAMPS\\\\n⋯\\\\nend\\\\ntime\\\\ntext tokens\\\\nbegin\\\\ntime\\\\nend\\\\ntime\\\\ntext tokens\\\\ntext tokens\\\\nVoice activity\\\\ndetection\\\\n(VAD)\\\\nCustom vocabulary /\\\\nprompting\\\\nTime-aligned transcription\\\\nText-only transcription\\\\n(allows dataset-specific fine-tuning)\\\\nX → English\\\\nTranslation \\\\nprevious\\\\ntext tokens\\\\nX → X\\\\nTranscription \\\\nLanguage\\\\nidentification\\\\nMLP\\\\nself attention\\\\nMLP\\\\nself attention\\\\nMLP\\\\nself attention\\\\nMLP\\\\ncross attention\\\\nself attention\\\\nMLP\\\\ncross attention\\\\nself attention\\\\nMLP\\\\ncross attention\\\\nself attention\\\\nTRANS-\\\\nCRIBE\\\\nFigure 1. All of these\\\\ntasks are jointly represented as a sequence of tokens to be predicted by the decoder, allowing for a single model to replace many different\\\\nstages of a traditional speech processing pipeline. Training Details\\\\nWe train a suite of models of various sizes in order to study\\\\nthe scaling properties of Whisper. Please see Table 1 for an\\\\noverview. We train with data parallelism across accelerators\\\\nusing FP16 with dynamic loss scaling and activation check-\\\\npointing (Griewank & Walther, 2000; Chen et al., 2016).\\\\nModels were trained with AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter,\\\\n2017) and gradient norm clipping (Pascanu et al., 2013)\\\\nwith a linear learning rate decay to zero after a warmup over\\\\nthe ﬁrst 2048 updates. A batch size of 256 segments was\\\\nused, and the models are trained for 220 updates which is\\\\nbetween two and three passes over the dataset. Due to only\\\\ntraining for a few epochs, over-ﬁtting is not a large concern,\\\\nand we do not use any data augmentation or regularization\\\\nand instead rely on the diversity contained within such a\\\\nlarge dataset to encourage generalization and robustness.\\\\nPlease see Appendix F for full training hyperparameters.3\\\\nDuring early development and evaluation we observed that\\\\nWhisper models had a tendency to transcribe plausible but\\\\nalmost always incorrect guesses for the names of speakers.\\\\nThis happens because many transcripts in the pre-training\\\\ndataset include the name of the person who is speaking,\\\\nencouraging the model to try to predict them, but this infor-\\\\nmation is only rarely inferable from only the most recent 30\\\\n3After the original release of Whisper, we trained an additional\\\\nLarge model (denoted V2) for 2.5X more epochs while adding\\\\nSpecAugment (Park et al., 2019), Stochastic Depth (Huang et al.,\\\\n2016), and BPE Dropout (Provilkov et al., 2019) for regularization.\\\\nReported results have been updated to this improved model unless\\\\notherwise speciﬁed.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 5 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n5\\\\nModel\\\\nLayers\\\\nWidth\\\\nHeads\\\\nParameters\\\\nTiny\\\\n4\\\\n384\\\\n6\\\\n39M\\\\nBase\\\\n6\\\\n512\\\\n8\\\\n74M\\\\nSmall\\\\n12\\\\n768\\\\n12\\\\n244M\\\\nMedium\\\\n24\\\\n1024\\\\n16\\\\n769M\\\\nLarge\\\\n32\\\\n1280\\\\n20\\\\n1550M\\\\nTable 1. To avoid this, we ﬁne-tune Whis-\\\\nper models brieﬂy on the subset of transcripts that do not\\\\ninclude speaker annotations which removes this behavior.\\\\n3. Experiments\\\\n3.1. Zero-shot Evaluation\\\\nThe goal of Whisper is to develop a single robust speech\\\\nprocessing system that works reliably without the need for\\\\ndataset speciﬁc ﬁne-tuning to achieve high-quality results\\\\non speciﬁc distributions. To study this capability, we re-\\\\nuse a wide set of existing speech processing datasets to\\\\ncheck whether Whisper is able to generalize well across\\\\ndomains, tasks, and languages. Instead of using the standard\\\\nevaluation protocol for these datasets, which include both\\\\na train and test split, we evaluate Whisper in a zero-shot\\\\nsetting without using any of the training data for each of\\\\nthese datasets so that we are measuring broad generalization.\\\\n3.2. Evaluation Metrics\\\\nSpeech recognition research typically evaluates and com-\\\\npares systems based on the word error rate (WER) metric.\\\\nHowever, WER, which is based on string edit distance, pe-\\\\nnalizes all differences between the model’s output and the\\\\nreference transcript including innocuous differences in tran-\\\\nscript style. As a result, systems that output transcripts that\\\\nwould be judged as correct by humans can still have a large\\\\nWER due to minor formatting differences. While this poses\\\\na problem for all transcribers, it is particularly acute for\\\\nzero-shot models like Whisper, which do not observe any\\\\nexamples of speciﬁc datasets transcript formats.\\\\nThis is not a novel observation; the development of evalua-\\\\ntion metrics that better correlate with human judgement is an\\\\nactive area of research, and while there are some promising\\\\nmethods, none have seen widespread adoption for speech\\\\nrecognition yet. We opt to address this problem with ex-\\\\ntensive standardization of text before the WER calculation\\\\nto minimize penalization of non-semantic differences. Our\\\\ntext normalizer was developed through iterative manual in-\\\\nspection to identify common patterns where naive WER\\\\npenalized Whisper models for an innocuous difference. Ap-\\\\npendix C includes full details. For several datasets, we\\\\nobserve WER drops of up to 50 percent usually due to a\\\\nquirk such as a dataset’s reference transcripts seperating\\\\ncontractions from words with whitespace. We caution this\\\\ndevelopment procedure comes at a risk of overﬁtting to the\\\\ntranscription style of Whisper models which we investigate\\\\nin Section 4.4. We are releasing the code for our text nor-\\\\nmalizer to allow for easy comparison and to help others\\\\nstudy the performance of speech recognition systems in\\\\nout-of-distribution settings.\\\\n3.3. English Speech Recognition\\\\nIn 2015, Deep Speech 2 (Amodei et al., 2015) reported\\\\na speech recognition system matched human-level perfor-\\\\nmance when transcribing the LibriSpeech test-clean split.\\\\nAs part of their analysis they concluded: “Given this result,\\\\nwe suspect that there is little room for a generic speech sys-\\\\ntem to further improve on clean read speech without further\\\\ndomain adaptation.” Yet seven years later the SOTA WER\\\\non LibriSpeech test-clean has dropped another 73% from\\\\ntheir 5.3% to 1.4% (Zhang et al., 2021), far below their re-\\\\nported human-level error rate of 5.8%. Despite this massive\\\\nand unanticipated further improvement in performance on\\\\nheld-out but in-distribution data, speech recognition mod-\\\\nels trained on LibriSpeech remain far above human error\\\\nrates when used in other settings. What explains this gap\\\\nbetween reportedly superhuman performance in-distribution\\\\nand subhuman performance out-of-distribution?\\\\nWe suspect a large part of this gap between human and\\\\nmachine behavior is due to conﬂating different capabilities\\\\nbeing measured by human and machine performance on\\\\na test set. This claim may seem confusing at ﬁrst; if both\\\\nhumans and machines are taking the same test, how can it be\\\\nthat different skills are being tested? The difference arises\\\\nnot in the testing but in how they trained for it. Humans are\\\\noften asked to perform a task given little to no supervision\\\\non the speciﬁc data distribution being studied. Thus human\\\\nperformance is a measure of out-of-distribution generaliza-\\\\ntion. But machine learning models are usually evaluated\\\\nafter training on a large amount of supervision from the\\\\nevaluation distribution, meaning that machine performance\\\\nis instead a measure of in-distribution generalization. While\\\\nboth humans and machines are being evaluated on the same\\\\ntest data, two quite different abilities are being measured\\\\ndue to a difference in train data.\\\\nWhisper models, which are trained on a broad and diverse\\\\ndistribution of audio and evaluated in a zero-shot setting,\\\\ncould potentially match human behavior much better than\\\\nexisting systems. To study whether this is the case (or\\\\nwhether the difference between machine and human per-\\\\nformance is due to yet-to-be-understood factors) we can\\\\ncompare Whisper models with both human performance\\\\nand standard ﬁne-tuned machine learning models and check\\\\nwhich they more closely match.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 6 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n6\\\\n0\\\\n1\\\\n2\\\\n3\\\\n4\\\\n5\\\\n6\\\\n7\\\\n8\\\\nWER on LibriSpeech dev-clean (%)\\\\n0\\\\n10\\\\n20\\\\n30\\\\n40\\\\n50\\\\nAverage WER on [Common Voice, CHiME-6, TED-LIUM] (%)\\\\nSupervised LibriSpeech models\\\\nZero-shot Whisper models\\\\nZero-shot Human (Alec)\\\\nIdeal robustness (y = x)\\\\nFigure 2. Zero-shot Whisper models close the gap to human\\\\nrobustness. Despite matching or outperforming a human on Lib-\\\\nriSpeech dev-clean, supervised LibriSpeech models make roughly\\\\ntwice as many errors as a human on other datasets demonstrating\\\\ntheir brittleness and lack of robustness. The estimated robustness\\\\nfrontier of zero-shot Whisper models, however, includes the 95%\\\\nconﬁdence interval for this particular human.\\\\nTo quantify this difference, we examine both overall ro-\\\\nbustness, that is average performance across many distribu-\\\\ntions/datasets, and effective robustness, introduced by Taori\\\\net al. (2020), which measures the difference in expected\\\\nperformance between a reference dataset, which is usually\\\\nin-distribution, and one or more out-of-distribution datasets.\\\\nA model with high effective robustness does better than\\\\nexpected on out-of-distribution datasets as a function of its\\\\nperformance on the reference dataset and approaches the\\\\nideal of equal performance on all datasets. For our analy-\\\\nsis, we use LibriSpeech as the reference dataset due to its\\\\ncentral role in modern speech recognition research and the\\\\navailability of many released models trained on it, which\\\\nallows for characterizing robustness behaviors. We use a\\\\nsuite of 12 other academic speech recognition datasets to\\\\nstudy out-of-distribution behaviors. Full details about these\\\\ndatasets can be found in Appendix A.\\\\nOur main ﬁndings are summarized in Figure 2 and Table 2.\\\\nAlthough the best zero-shot Whisper model has a relatively\\\\nunremarkable LibriSpeech clean-test WER of 2.5, which\\\\nis roughly the performance of modern supervised baseline\\\\nor the mid-2019 state of the art, zero-shot Whisper models\\\\nhave very different robustness properties than supervised\\\\nLibriSpeech models and out-perform all benchmarked Lib-\\\\nriSpeech models by large amounts on other datasets. Long-form Transcription\\\\nWhisper models are trained on 30-second audio chunks and\\\\ncannot consume longer audio inputs at once. This is not a\\\\nproblem with most academic datasets comprised of short\\\\nutterances but presents challenges in real-world applications\\\\nwhich often require transcribing minutes- or hours-long au-\\\\ndio. We developed a strategy to perform buffered transcrip-\\\\ntion of long audio by consecutively transcribing 30-second\\\\nsegments of audio and shifting the window according to the\\\\ntimestamps predicted by the model. We observed that it\\\\nis crucial to have beam search and temperature scheduling\\\\nbased on the repetitiveness and the log probability of the\\\\nmodel predictions in order to reliably transcribe long audio.\\\\nThe full procedure is described in Section 4.5.\\\\nWe evaluate the long-form transcription performance on\\\\nseven datasets consisting of speech recordings of various\\\\nlengths and recording conditions, to cover as diverse a data\\\\ndistribution as possible. Full details about the long-form datasets can\\\\nbe found in Appendix A.\\\\nWe compare the performance with open-source models as\\\\nwell as 4 commercial ASR services. Comparison with Human Performance\\\\nBecause of ambiguous or indistinct speech as well as la-\\\\nbeling errors, there are different levels of irreducible error\\\\nin each dataset, and with WER metrics from ASR systems\\\\nalone it is difﬁcult to make sense of how much room for\\\\nimprovement exists in each dataset. To quantify how close\\\\nWhisper’s performance is to the human performance, we se-\\\\nlected 25 recordings from the Kincaid46 dataset and used 5\\\\nservices to obtain transcripts produced by professional tran-\\\\nscribers, among which one provides computer-assisted tran-\\\\nscription and the other four are entirely human-transcribed.\\\\nThe audio selection covers various recording conditions\\\\nsuch as scripted and unscripted broadcast, telephone and\\\\nVoIP calls, and meetings. Figure 7 shows the distribution\\\\nof per-example WERs and aggregate WER across the 25\\\\nrecordings, where the computer-assisted service has the\\\\nlowest aggregate WER that is 1.15% point better than Whis-\\\\nper’s, and the pure-human performance is only a fraction\\\\nof a percentage point better than Whisper’s. These results\\\\nindicate that Whisper’s English ASR performance is not\\\\nperfect but very close to human-level accuracy.\\\\n4. Analysis and Ablations\\\\n4.1. Model Scaling\\\\nA large amount of the promise in weakly supervised train-\\\\ning approaches is their potential to use datasets much larger\\\\nthan those in traditional supervised learning. However, this\\\\ncomes with the cost of using data that is possibly much\\\\nnoisier and lower quality than gold-standard supervision.\\\\nA concern with this approach is that although it may look\\\\npromising to begin with, the performance of models trained\\\\non this kind of data may saturate at the inherent quality level\\\\nof the dataset, which could be far below human level. A re-\\\\nlated concern is that as capacity and compute spent training\\\\non the dataset increases, models may learn to exploit the\\\\nWhisper\\\\nA\\\\nB\\\\nC\\\\nD\\\\nE\\\\nF\\\\nG\\\\nH\\\\nI\\\\n ASR \\\\n          \\\\n human transcription \\\\n \\\\n          computer-assisted\\\\n0\\\\n5\\\\n10\\\\n15\\\\n20\\\\n25\\\\n30\\\\nWord Error Rate (%)\\\\nFigure 7. Strategies for Reliable Long-form Transcription\\\\nTranscribing long-form audio using Whisper relies on ac-\\\\ncurate prediction of the timestamp tokens to determine the\\\\namount to shift the model’s 30-second audio context win-\\\\ndow by, and inaccurate transcription in one window may\\\\nnegatively impact transcription in the subsequent windows.\\\\nWe have developed a set of heuristics that help avoid fail-\\\\nure cases of long-form transcription, which is applied in\\\\nthe results reported in sections 3.8 and 3.9. First, we use\\\\nbeam search with 5 beams using the log probability as the\\\\nscore function, to reduce repetition looping which happens\\\\nmore frequently in greedy decoding. We start with tem-\\\\nperature 0, i.e. always selecting the tokens with the high-\\\\nest probability, and increase the temperature by 0.2 up to\\\\n1.0 when either the average log probability over the gen-\\\\nerated tokens is lower than −1 or the generated text has a\\\\ngzip compression rate higher than 2.4. Providing the tran-\\\\nscribed text from the preceding window as previous-text\\\\nconditioning when the applied temperature is below 0.5\\\\nfurther improves the performance. We found that the proba-\\\\nbility of the <|nospeech|> token alone is not sufﬁcient\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 13 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n13\\\\nTED-LIUM3\\\\nMeanwhile\\\\nKincaid46\\\\nRev16\\\\nEarnings-21\\\\nEarnings-22\\\\nCORAAL\\\\nAverage\\\\nGreedy decoding only\\\\n3.95 5.16 9.69 11.7 10.7 14.0 22.0\\\\n11.0\\\\n+ Beam search\\\\n4.16 5.71 9.42 11.5 10.2 13.4 20.0\\\\n10.6\\\\n+ Temperature fallback\\\\n4.16 5.71 9.42 11.5 10.2 13.4 20.0\\\\n10.6\\\\n+ Voice activity detection\\\\n3.56 4.61 9.45 11.4 10.1 13.2 19.4\\\\n10.2\\\\n+ Previous text conditioning\\\\n3.42 6.16 8.72 11.0 9.63 13.3 18.1\\\\n10.0\\\\n+ Initial timestamp constraint\\\\n3.51 5.26 8.41 11.5 9.73 12.6 19.1\\\\n10.0\\\\nTable 7. Finally, to avoid a fail-\\\\nure mode where the model ignores the ﬁrst few words in\\\\nthe input, we constrained the initial timestamp token to be\\\\nbetween 0.0 and 1.0 second. Table 7 shows that adding each\\\\nof the interventions above incrementally reduces the WER\\\\noverall, but not evenly across the dataset. These heuristics\\\\nserve as a workaround for the noisy predictions of the model,\\\\nand more research would be needed to further improve the\\\\nreliability of long-form decoding.\\\\n5. Related Work\\\\nScaling Speech Recognition\\\\nA consistent theme across\\\\nspeech recognition research has been documenting the bene-\\\\nﬁts of scaling compute, models, and datasets. Early work ap-\\\\nplying deep learning to speech recognition found improved\\\\nperformance with model depth and size and leveraged GPU\\\\nacceleration to make training these larger models tractable\\\\n(Mohamed et al., 2009). Further research demonstrated that\\\\nthe beneﬁt of deep learning approaches to speech recogni-\\\\ntion increased with dataset size, improving from being only\\\\ncompetitive with prior GMM-HMM systems when using\\\\njust 3 hours of TIMIT training data for phone recognition\\\\nto achieving a 30% word error rate reduction when trained\\\\non the 2,000 hour Switchboard dataset (Seide et al., 2011).\\\\nLiao et al. (2013) is an early example of leveraging weakly\\\\nsupervised learning to increase the size of a deep learn-\\\\ning based speech recognition dataset by over 1,000 hours.\\\\nThese trends continued with Deep Speech 2 (Amodei et al.,\\\\n2015) being a notable system developing high-throughput\\\\ndistributed training across 16 GPUs and scaling to 12,000\\\\nhours of training data while demonstrating continuing im-\\\\nprovements at that scale. By leveraging semi-supervised\\\\npre-training, Narayanan et al. (2018) were able to grow\\\\ndataset size much further and study training on 162,000\\\\nhours of labeled audio. More recent work has explored\\\\nbillion-parameter models (Zhang et al., 2020) and using up\\\\nto 1,000,000 hours of training data (Zhang et al., 2021).\\\\nMultitask Learning\\\\nMultitask learning (Caruana, 1997)\\\\nhas been studied for a long time. In speech recognition,\\\\nmulti-lingual models have been explored for well over a\\\\ndecade (Schultz & Kirchhoff, 2006). An inspirational and\\\\nfoundational work in NLP exploring multi-task learning\\\\nwith a single model is Collobert et al. (2011). Multitask\\\\nlearning in the sequence-to-sequence framework (Sutskever\\\\net al., 2014) using multiple encoders and decoders was in-\\\\nvestigated in Luong et al. (2015). The use of language codes\\\\nwith a shared encoder/decoder architecture was ﬁrst demon-\\\\nstrated for machine translation by Johnson et al. (2017),\\\\nremoving the need for separate encoders and decoders. This\\\\napproach was simpliﬁed further into the “text-to-text” frame-\\\\nwork of McCann et al. (2018) and popularized by its success\\\\nwith large transformer language models in the work of Rad-\\\\nford et al. (2019) and Raffel et al. (2020). Toshniwal et al.\\\\n(2018) demonstrated jointly training a modern deep learn-\\\\ning speech recognition system on several languages with a\\\\nsingle model, and Pratap et al. (2020a) scaled this line of\\\\nwork signiﬁcantly to 50 languages with a billion-parameter\\\\nmodel. MUTE (Wang et al., 2020c) and mSLAM (Bapna\\\\net al., 2022) studied joint training over both text and speech\\\\nlanguage tasks, demonstrating transfer between them.\\\\nRobustness\\\\nThe question of how effectively models trans-\\\\nfer and how robust they are to distribution shift and other\\\\ntypes of perturbations has long been studied and is actively\\\\nbeing researched across many ﬁelds of machine learning.\\\\nTorralba & Efros (2011) highlighted the lack of generaliza-\\\\ntion of machine learning models between datasets over a\\\\ndecade ago. Many other works have shown and continu-\\\\nally reiterated how despite high performance on IID test\\\\nsets, machine learning models can still make many mistakes\\\\nwhen evaluated in even slightly different settings (Lake et al.,\\\\n2017; Jia & Liang, 2017; Alcorn et al., 2019; Barbu et al.,\\\\n2019; Recht et al., 2019). More recently, Taori et al. (2020)\\\\nstudied the robustness of image classiﬁcation models, and\\\\nMiller et al. (2020) investigated this for question-answering\\\\nmodels. A key ﬁnding has been that multi-domain train-\\\\ning increases robustness and generalization as discussed in\\\\nthe Introduction. This ﬁnding has been replicated across\\\\nmany ﬁelds in addition to speech recognition including NLP\\\\n(Hendrycks et al., 2020) and computer vision (Radford et al.,\\\\n2021).\\\\n6. Limitations and Future Work\\\\nFrom our experimental results, analyses, and ablations, we\\\\nhave noted several limitations and areas for future work.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 14 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n14\\\\nImproved decoding strategies.\\\\nAs we have scaled Whis-\\\\nper, we have observed that larger models have made steady\\\\nand reliable progress on reducing perception-related errors\\\\nsuch as confusing similar-sounding words. Many remaining\\\\nerrors, particularly in long-form transcription seem more\\\\nstubborn in nature and decidedly non-human/perceptual.\\\\nThey are a combination of failure modes of seq2seq mod-\\\\nels, language models, and text-audio alignment and include\\\\nproblems such as getting stuck in repeat loops, not tran-\\\\nscribing the ﬁrst or last few words of an audio segment, or\\\\ncomplete hallucination where the model will output a tran-\\\\nscript entirely unrelated to the actual audio. Although the\\\\ndecoding details discussed in Section 4.5 help signiﬁcantly,\\\\nwe suspect ﬁne-tuning Whisper models on a high-quality\\\\nsupervised dataset and/or using reinforcement learning to\\\\nmore directly optimize for decoding performance could help\\\\nfurther reduce these errors.\\\\nIncrease Training Data For Lower-Resource Languages\\\\nAs Figure 3 shows, Whisper’s speech recognition perfor-\\\\nmance is still quite poor on many languages. The same\\\\nanalysis suggests a clear route for improvement since perfor-\\\\nmance on a language is very well predicted by the amount\\\\nof training data for the language. Since our pre-training\\\\ndataset is currently very English-heavy due to biases of\\\\nour data collection pipeline, which sourced primarily from\\\\nEnglish-centric parts of the internet, most languages have\\\\nless than 1000 hours of training data. A targeted effort at in-\\\\ncreasing the amount of data for these rarer languages could\\\\nresult in a large improvement to average speech recognition\\\\nperformance even with only a small increase in our overall\\\\ntraining dataset size.\\\\nStudying ﬁne-tuning\\\\nIn this work, we have focused on\\\\nthe robustness properties of speech processing systems and\\\\nas a result only studied the zero-shot transfer performance\\\\nof Whisper. While this is a crucial setting to study due to it\\\\nbeing representative of general reliability, for many domains\\\\nwhere high-quality supervised speech data does exist, it is\\\\nlikely that results can be improved further by ﬁne-tuning.\\\\nAn additional beneﬁt of studying ﬁne-tuning is that it allows\\\\nfor direct comparisons with prior work since it is a much\\\\nmore common evaluation setting.\\\\nStudying the impact of Language Models on Robustness\\\\nAs argued in the introduction, we suspect that Whisper’s\\\\nrobustness is partially due to its strong decoder, which is an\\\\naudio conditional language model. It’s currently unclear to\\\\nwhat degree the beneﬁts of Whisper stem from training its\\\\nencoder, decoder, or both. This could be studied by either\\\\nablating various design components of Whisper, such as\\\\ntraining a decoder-less CTC model, or by studying how the\\\\nperformance of existing speech recognition encoders such\\\\nas wav2vec 2.0 change when used together with a language\\\\nmodel.\\\\nAdding Auxiliary Training Objectives\\\\nWhisper departs\\\\nnoticeably from most recent state-of-the-art speech recog-\\\\nnition systems due to the lack of unsupervised pre-training\\\\nor self-teaching methods. While we have not found them\\\\nnecessary to achieve good performance, it is possible that\\\\nthe results could be further improved by incorporating this.\\\\n7. Conclusion\\\\nWhisper suggests that scaling weakly supervised pre-\\\\ntraining has been underappreciated so far in speech recogni-\\\\ntion research. We achieve our results without the need for\\\\nthe self-supervision and self-training techniques that have\\\\nbeen a mainstay of recent large-scale speech recognition\\\\nwork and demonstrate how simply training on a large and\\\\ndiverse supervised dataset and focusing on zero-shot trans-\\\\nfer can signiﬁcantly improve the robustness of a speech\\\\nrecognition system.\\\\nACKNOWLEDGMENTS\\\\nWe’d like to thank the millions of people who were involved\\\\nin creating the data used by Whisper. Text Standardization\\\\nSince Whisper may output any UTF-8 string rather than a restricted set of graphemes, the rules for text standardization need\\\\nto be more intricate and comprehensive than those deﬁned on e.g. ASCII characters. We perform the following steps to\\\\nnormalize English texts in different styles into a standardized form, which is a best-effort attempt to penalize only when a\\\\nword error is caused by actually mistranscribing a word, and not by formatting or punctuation differences.\\\\n1. Remove any phrases between matching brackets ([, ]).\\\\n2. Remove any phrases between matching parentheses ((, )).\\\\n3. Remove any of the following words: hmm, mm, mhm, mmm, uh, um\\\\n4. Remove whitespace characters that comes before an apostrophe ’\\\\n5. Convert standard or informal contracted forms of English into the original form.\\\\n6. Remove commas (,) between digits\\\\n7. Remove periods (.) not followed by numbers\\\\n8. Remove symbols as well as diacritics from the text, where symbols are the characters with the Unicode category\\\\nstarting with M, S, or P, except period, percent, and currency symbols that may be detected in the next step.\\\\n9. Detect any numeric expressions of numbers and currencies and replace with a form using Arabic numbers, e.g. “Ten\\\\nthousand dollars” →“$10000”.\\\\n10. Convert British spellings into American spellings.\\\\n11. Remove remaining symbols that are not part of any numeric expressions.\\\\n12. Replace any successive whitespace characters with a space.\\\\nA different, language-speciﬁc set of transformations would be needed to equivalently normalize non-English text, but due to\\\\nour lack of linguistic knowledge to build such normalizers for all languages, we resort to the following basic standardization\\\\nfor non-English text:\\\\n1. Remove any phrases between matching brackets ([, ]).\\\\n2. Remove any phrases between matching parentheses ((, )).\\\\n3. Replace any markers, symbols, and punctuation characters with a space, i.e. when the Unicode category of each\\\\ncharacter in the NFKC-normalized string starts with M, S, or P.\\\\n4. make the text lowercase.\\\\n5. replace any successive whitespace characters with a space.\\\\nAdditionally, we put a space between every letter for the languages that do not use spaces to separate words, namely Chinese,\\\\nJapanese, Thai, Lao, and Burmese, effectively measuring the character error rate instead.\\\\nWe note that the above is an imperfect solution, and it will sometimes produce unintended and unexpected outputs. We do\\\\nnot claim that the text format resulting from the above is more “correct” in any measure. Rather, the procedures above are\\\\ndesigned to better distinguish between innocuous differences in wording and genuine mistranscriptions. Python code for\\\\nthe standardization procedures above is available as part of our code and model release to facilitate future iterations and\\\\nimprovements on text standardization.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 22 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n22\\\\nD. Token、声学块与播放时钟\\\\n\\\\n语音服务把两条时钟接起来：模型在离散声学帧上生成 codec token，客户端按采样时钟连续播放波形。平均 token/s 或音频秒/秒只说明其中一段；首个可播放样本、稳态不断音、打断后静音和尾部完整性还要经过条件等待、声学解码、上下文窗口、网络与客户端缓冲。\\\\n\\\\n## 生成对象与播放时钟\\\\n\\\\n设采样率 f_s（Hz），声学帧率 f_a（帧/s），每块 N_f 个声学帧，codebook 数为 C。声学帧 j 名义上覆盖时间区间 [j/f_a,(j+1)/f_a)。块 b 覆盖帧 bN_f,...,(b+1)N_f−1，名义时长为\\\\n\\\\nD = N_f / f_a。\\\\n\\\\n若 f_s/f_a 不是整数，不能假设每帧恰好整数个样本。以有理数边界\\\\n\\\\ns_b = floor(b N_f f_s / f_a)\\\\n\\\\n定义块 b 的逻辑样本区间 [s_b,s_{b+1})。s_b 单调不减；实际块长 s_{b+1}−s_b 只能按该有理边界取相邻整数。若每块都先取整成同一个长度再累加，长请求会逐渐偏离声学时间轴。输出样本 y[s] 的 s 是请求内逻辑 sample offset，不是网络 chunk 序号。\\\\n\\\\n设 token 记为 x_{c,j}，c 为 codebook，j 为声学帧。一个块通常需要其必需 codebook 的完整帧集合才能解码；若模型有 codebook 延迟、多 token 帧或先文本后声学的 track，实际所需集合由 checkpoint 契约给出，不能把“一个 codebook 一个 token”当作所有模型的事实。\\\\n\\\\n请求状态至少区分：\\\\n\\\\n| 状态 | 已经知道的事实 | 不能由它推出的事实 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| CODE_READY(b) | 块 b 的必需 token 已生成并带版本 | mel 或波形已经稳定 |\\\\n| DECODED(b) | 解码器在块 b 的逻辑样本区间产出了可提交波形 | 客户端已经收到或播放 |\\\\n| SENT(b) | 块已交给发送路径 | 远端已经消费，播放时钟已前进 |\\\\n| PLAYED(P) | 客户端已播放到 sample offset P | 旧代次在途块不会再到达 |\\\\n| CANCELLED(epoch) | 该代次不再允许新提交 | 在途 compute、传输和旧音频已经消失 |\\\\n\\\\n所有块都带请求 ID、代次、块号、起始 sample offset 和格式身份。服务端的“已生成”不等于“已解码”，更不等于“用户已听到”。\\\\n\\\\nQwen2.5-Omni 的固定报告给出一条具体组合：Thinker 产生高层表示和文本，Talker 以流式方式接收这些表示及文本 token 的 embedding，产生语音 token；报告中的 qwen-tts-tokenizer 可用 causal audio decoder 流式解码。报告另描述 Flow-Matching DiT 把 code 块转成 mel，再由修改的 BigVGAN 生成波形。DiT 的滑动窗口为 4 个块，包含 2 个 lookback、当前块和 1 个 lookahead。报告还说明语音生成不要求与文本做词级或时间戳级对齐。这里支持的是该报告描述的路径；具体 checkpoint 的 token 排列、求解器步数和声码器重叠仍要分别核对。\\\\n\\\\n## 合法性与可解码块\\\\n\\\\n设 L 为左上下文块数，A 为右 lookahead 块数。块 b 可进入声学解码的必要条件可写为\\\\n\\\\nCodeOK(b) ∧ ContextOK(b)，\\\\n\\\\n其中 CodeOK(b) 表示 bN_f 到 (b+1)N_f−1 的必需 codebook 帧均已发布且版本一致；ContextOK(b) 表示 b−L 到 b+A 的窗口均有合法来源。窗口边界不能静默省略：\\\\n\\\\n- k<0 时，只有模型契约明确给出的首块处理（零填充、重复首帧、更短窗口或专用首块）可以作为左上下文；没有这种规则时，不能把不存在的块当作真实上下文。\\\\n- k 超过最后真实 code 块时，只有模型明确允许的尾部填充或 flush 才能补足右上下文；否则应等待、拒绝或返回上下文不足，而不是把补零后的结果当作等价稳态输出。\\\\n- 某个中间块未 CODE_READY 时，后面即使已有更远块，也不能跳过依赖直接解码当前块。\\\\n\\\\n由此得到三条不同事实：token 已生成、块可解码、样本可提交。多 codebook 生成的延迟排列、文本条件是否已产生、声码器是否需要重叠窗口，都可能使 CODE_READY(b) 为真而 DecodeReady(b) 为假。lookahead 是函数和质量契约，不是可以任意删减的性能参数；缩短 lookahead 后必须重新验证内容、音色、韵律和接缝。\\\\n\\\\n采样几何也必须合法。若 f_s/f_a 为有理数但非整数，必须保存累计 sample offset 或使用有理数边界；不能用网络块数推算采样位置，也不能在 EOS 前后任意补静音来掩盖长度不足。EOS 只表示不会再有新的真实 code，不表示尾部上下文已经自动满足。尾部处理必须按模型允许的规则完成；没有合法尾部规则时，应把结果标成上下文不足或失败，不能把未稳定样本当成交付音频。\\\\n\\\\n同一请求的所有块还必须共享代次和格式身份。旧代次的迟到块即使 sample offset 看起来连续，也不能写入新响应；客户端已经播放的样本无法撤销，协议要区分“已确认播放”和“已发送但未播放”。\\\\n\\\\n## 从 codec token 到可播放样本\\\\n\\\\n下面的参考算法把机制写成可检查的数据流。实际 checkpoint 可能使用不同的 flow 求解器、codebook 排列或声码器重叠规则；替换这些局部函数时，块窗口、样本边界、原子发布和尾部检查仍应保留。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nFUNCTION DecodeReady(req,b)\\\\n输入：请求 req，块号 b\\\\n输出：是否可进入 DiT/vocoder\\\\n1. 若 b<0 或 b 不属于当前代次：返回 false；\\\\n2. 对每个模型要求的 codebook c 和帧 j∈[bN_f,(b+1)N_f)：\\\\n       若 x_{c,j} 未发布或版本不符：返回 false；\\\\n3. 对 k=b−L,...,b+A：\\\\n       若 k<0：仅当 startup_policy 明确给出初始左上下文时继续，否则返回 false；\\\\n       若 k>last_code_block：仅当 end_policy 明确允许尾部填充或 flush 时继续，否则返回 false；\\\\n       若 0≤k≤last_code_block 且 CODE_READY(k) 为假：返回 false；\\\\n4. 若 b 的 sample 边界 s_b,s_{b+1} 与请求几何不一致：返回 false；\\\\n5. 返回 true。\\\\n\\\\nFUNCTION FlowMatchBlock(z0,t0,...,tK,context_blocks)\\\\n输入：该块初始 latent 或噪声 z0，离散或连续时间表 t0..tK，窗口上下文\\\\n输出：该块 mel 表示\\\\n1. z←z0；\\\\n2. 对 k=0..K−1：\\\\n       v←DiT(z,t_k,context_blocks)；\\\\n       z←z+(t_{k+1}−t_k)v；\\\\n3. 按模型规定的输出投影得到 mel；\\\\n4. 返回 mel。\\\\n注：这是显式积分的参考数据流；若 checkpoint 使用不同 solver，替换时间表和更新式，不改变块依赖。\\\\n\\\\nFUNCTION PublishStableBlock(req,b,wav,origin,left_overlap)\\\\n输入：解码器原始波形、全局起点、左重叠长度\\\\n输出：可提交的块波形或长度/偏移错误\\\\n1. 将 wav 的位置 i 映射到全局 sample index origin+i；\\\\n2. 只保留满足 s_b≤origin+i<s_{b+1} 的样本；\\\\n3. 若保留数不等于 s_{b+1}−s_b：返回 BLOCK_LENGTH_MISMATCH；\\\\n4. 若首样本全局 index 不等于 req.emit：返回 GAP_OR_DUPLICATE；\\\\n5. 原子发布 DECODED(b)，把 req.emit 设为 s_{b+1}；\\\\n6. 返回成功。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n主推进算法把生成、解码和终止放在同一状态机里。生成块可以提前于解码，但一个块只有在全部必需 token 和上下文发布后才能被解码；解码结果只有在按 sample offset 裁剪后才能进入发送路径。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nALGORITHM AdvanceSpeech(req,budget)\\\\n输入：已初始化请求、当前时间片预算\\\\n输出：状态进展、等待原因、暂停或终态\\\\n1. 若 req.epoch 不是当前代次或已取消：不发布新块；在允许排空后返回 CANCELLED；\\\\n2. 若 state=CONDITIONING：\\\\n       若文本、语义、说话人或其他条件未就绪：返回 WAIT_CONDITION；\\\\n       初始化 Talker/codec 状态、重叠状态和有界队列；state←GENERATING；\\\\n3. 重复直到预算用尽：\\\\n   a. 若 req.next_code<req.code_end 且预算允许：\\\\n          b←req.next_code；\\\\n          按模型实际 track/codebook 顺序生成块 b 所需 token；\\\\n          只有全部必需 token、版本和 block 身份齐备才发布 CODE_READY(b)；\\\\n          req.next_code←b+1；计入生成工作；\\\\n   b. b←req.next_decode；\\\\n          若 b 的 code 尚未齐备：返回 WAIT_CODE；\\\\n          若 not DecodeReady(req,b)：返回 WAIT_CONTEXT；\\\\n          mel_b←FlowMatchBlock(..., context b−L..b+A)；\\\\n          wav_b←VocoderBlock(mel_b,overlap_state,end_policy)；\\\\n          PublishStableBlock(req,b,wav_b,decoder_origin,left_overlap)；\\\\n          req.next_decode←b+1；计入 flow/vocoder 工作；\\\\n   c. 若 req.code_end 且 next_decode 已覆盖最后块：\\\\n          按终止策略 flush 尾部；若尾部合法且发送队列允许，state←DONE 并返回；\\\\n          否则返回 NEED_END_POLICY；\\\\n   d. 若本轮既不能生成也不能解码且没有合法终态：\\\\n          返回当前 WAIT_CODE、WAIT_CONTEXT 或 WAIT_SEND；\\\\n4. 保存 cursor、overlap、solver 状态和未提交 token，返回 PAUSED_BUDGET。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n正确性不变量是：每个已提交块的长度等于其逻辑样本区间；相邻块的 sample offset 连续；旧代次不能写入新请求；部分生成的 code 块和部分解码的波形不出现在消费者可见的连续流中。首块缺少真实左上下文时，必须使用显式 startup_policy；最后一块缺少右 lookahead 时，必须使用显式 end_policy。没有这两条策略，算法不能把首尾样本静默补成稳态块。\\\\n\\\\n## 供给、缓冲与调度\\\\n\\\\n设客户端在 A_k 时刻收到第 k 个完整可播放块，块时长为 D，播放开始时刻为 T_0。若选择先积 B_0 秒再播放，则 T_0=A_0+B_0。第 k 块的名义播放 deadline 是\\\\n\\\\nd_k = T_0 + kD。\\\\n\\\\n忽略块内解码和播放器内部重采样时，A_k>d_k 意味着播放队列在该块之前已经耗尽；等价地，按连续速率写，缓冲 B(t) 满足 dB/dt=a(t)−1，平均 a>1 不排除短时 a<1 造成欠载。初始缓冲降低欠载概率，却增加首可播放样本时间、取消后的尾音和内存占用。\\\\n\\\\n服务端调度应使用播放 deadline，而不是只最大化整段音频/秒。块 b 需要 b+A 的 code 上下文才能解码；若 C_{b+A} 是该上下文完成时间，Q_b 是 flow 解码时间，V_b 是声码器时间，N_b 是发送时间，则在串行近似下需要\\\\n\\\\nC_{b+A} + Q_b + V_b + N_b ≤ T_0 + bD − margin。\\\\n\\\\n若这些阶段可以重叠，应改用实际依赖图和共享资源的关键路径，不能把可重叠时间全部相加，也不能只取最大值而忽略同一设备上的争用。跨请求聚批分别发生在 Talker、flow step 和 vocoder；等待一个更大 batch 可能先耗尽某个会话的客户端缓冲，所以 batch 形成时间本身要进入 deadline。\\\\n\\\\n一个设计算例（不是实测）：f_s=24 kHz，f_a=50 Hz，N_f=10，则 D=200 ms，S_b=4800 个样本；24 kHz、单声道、16-bit PCM 的该块为 9600 字节，400 ms 缓冲为 19200 字节。设 code 生成 500 帧/s，A=1，flow 与 vocoder 合计 25 ms/块，发送 5 ms，且条件已就绪、各阶段串行。首块需要当前块加一个 lookahead，共 20 帧=40 ms；服务端首块可发送时间为 40+25+5=70 ms。稳态每块只新增 10 帧=20 ms，加 25+5=50 ms 供给 200 ms 音频，串行资源占用为 50/200=25%。若客户端先积 100 ms 再播，首样本约 70+100=170 ms；若条件还要等待 150 ms，服务端首块约 220 ms，播放再按缓冲策略推后。若某块 flow 排队 180 ms，单块会超过 D，平均 25% 不能保证不断音。\\\\n\\\\n网络压缩可以降低传输字节，却不改变声音代表的播放时长。测客户端实际收到完整可播放块的时间和累计 sample offset，不能用服务器 token 完成时间代替声音开始时间。\\\\n\\\\n## 成本与资源账\\\\n\\\\n计算成本至少分四类。第一，code token 生成：若每个声学帧每个 codebook 产生一个 token，则每秒约 C f_a 个预测；自回归依赖、采样和状态更新仍按模型实际 track 计。第二，flow 解码：窗口内有 T_W 个 token 时，单个 flow step 的 self-attention 约为 O(T_W²d)，线性投影约为 O(T_W d²)，再加条件 cross-attention；K 步合计还要乘 K。Qwen2.5-Omni 报告的窗口是 4 个块；不同 checkpoint 的 T_W、d、K 不同。第三，vocoder：按输出样本数 S_b、卷积核、通道和重叠窗口计；固定感受野的流式声码器每次仍需处理边界上下文。第四，主机侧封包、重采样、格式转换和队列管理。\\\\n\\\\n访存与驻留分别计：code ring 约为 C N_f W_ring 个 token 的存储；mel 块按 M 个 mel 帧和特征宽度计；波形块按 S_b×声道×每样本字节计；flow 激活、声码器 overlap、模型权重和 Talker 自回归状态另列。共享权重只计一次；不能把每个请求的权重副本和共享页重复相加。若 decoder 需要 L 个左块和 A 个右块，窗口驻留至少覆盖这些块及其 overlap；窗口越大，抗边界和音质可能更好，但驻留和重复计算增加。\\\\n\\\\n通信账要区分逻辑音频、编码后字节和网络事务。24 kHz 单声道 16-bit PCM 的稳态逻辑码率为 24000×16=384000 bit/s，即 384 kbit/s；200 ms 块为 9600 字节。编码压缩、容器、重传和协议头另行计入。同步账包括条件就绪、code 块发布、flow 完成、vocoder 完成、发送完成和客户端开始播放；这些是不同事件，不能用一个“首包”字段代替。准备账包括首块左上下文、说话人条件、codec 初始状态和可能的解码器预热。\\\\n\\\\n若阶段共享同一设备，串行总时间可能接近各项之和；若流水重叠，稳态吞吐由最慢阶段和共享资源决定，而首包仍受 lookahead 和启动依赖约束。一个阶段计算量下降但队列或传输成为瓶颈时，端到端首包和欠载不一定改善。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化与放弃路径\\\\n\\\\n| 变化 | 可以保留 | 必须重新检查或放弃 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| N_f 变小 | 同一套 sample offset 和 deadline 记账 | 每块调用数、边界处理、lookahead 占比和模型上下文改变；质量与实时率要重测 |\\\\n| f_s 提高 | 声学帧时长和 token 语义可保留 | 波形字节、声码器样本工作、网络码率和客户端缓冲字节改变 |\\\\n| f_a 改变 | 用 D=N_f/f_a 重算播放时钟 | code token 速率、lookahead 墙钟时间和训练/推理契约改变 |\\\\n| codebook 数增加 | 块窗口和 sample offset 规则 | token 生成、code ring、凑齐可解码块的时间和显存改变 |\\\\n| lookahead 减小 | 原 flow/vocoder 数学形式 | 首包可能提前，但上下文、接缝和内容质量改变；无模型允许时不能做 |\\\\n| flow 步数减少 | 每步的 solver 数据流 | 计算下降但求解误差和音质改变，必须独立评估，不能记作免费加速 |\\\\n| 更小 batch 或更大 batch | 每请求状态身份 | 聚批等待、设备利用率和尾延迟改变；大 batch 可能先耗尽播放缓冲 |\\\\n| EOS 提前或尾部不足 | 已提交块和 sample offset 不变 | 只能使用声明的尾部规则；否则应报告上下文不足或失败 |\\\\n| 网络抖动增加 | 声学块时长和逻辑码率 | 需要更大客户端缓冲、不同发送策略或 deadline 调度；单纯提高平均吞吐不够 |\\\\n| 模型或 codec 版本改变 | 请求 ID 和外部事件边界 | codec 状态、overlap、token 语义和声码器权重身份失效，旧缓存不能沿用 |\\\\n\\\\n选择反转的典型条件：离线生成可以等完整条件、用较大块和较高求解步数换取效率与质量；实时对话则需要更早的首可播放样本、按 deadline 调度和明确打断语义。若模型不支持所需流式块，继续缩小网络 chunk 只是把同一段非因果计算切碎，不会产生合法的低延迟声学输出。若 code 生成长期快于实时而 vocoder 是瓶颈，增加 code 并行度的收益有限；反之若 flow 排队主导，减少 code 延迟也不能消除欠载。\\\\n\\\\n打断时，旧代次不再接收新块，取消未提交的模型工作，并让在途 compute、传输、codec 状态和 overlap 安全结束。客户端也要丢弃尚未播放的旧代次数据；仅服务端停止生成，已缓冲音频仍会继续播放。已播放样本无法撤销，协议要记录最后确认的 sample offset 和新响应从何处开始。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 区分实验与修正方向 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 首音频很晚，但 code token/s 很高 | 条件等待；lookahead 不足；flow/vocoder 排队；网络或客户端缓冲 | 在同一请求记录条件就绪、CODE_READY(b+A)、flow 完成、vocoder 完成、发送、客户端到达和播放事件；先预置条件，再单独改变合法块大小或 buffer。若 code 完成早而播放晚，不能把原因归给 token 生成 |\\\\n| 平均供给大于实时，仍偶发断音 | 到达突发；单块排队；初始缓冲不足；尾部或重传 | 记录每块 lead=A_k−d_k 和队列长度，比较不同 buffer 与到达轨迹；平均实时率下降不能替代尾部欠载统计 |\\\\n| 块边界重复、缺口或 click | overlap 未裁；sample offset 漂移；resampler 边界错误；重传重复 | 用已知脉冲或递增 sample 序列逐块核对全局 offset 和长度；负对照故意把左 overlap 再发一次，检查器必须拒绝 |\\\\n| 减小块后音质变差 | 上下文窗口缩短；边界调用增多；求解步数改变；补零策略 | 固定求解器和权重，只在模型支持的块范围改变块；再固定块改变步数。若质量随步数变化，不能全归因于块大小 |\\\\n| 打断后仍听到旧回复 | 客户端未播放旧缓冲；在途 vocoder/网络块迟到；代次未隔离 | 在生成、解码、发送、客户端缓冲四个位置分别注入取消，检查旧代次是否还能提交或播放；只停服务端不足以保证静音 |\\\\n| batch 提高吞吐但欠载增加 | 聚批等待；资源争用；batch 内的长尾块 | 记录 batch 形成时间、最早 deadline 和每请求 lead；若 deadline 已过才凑批，应缩小等待或改按 deadline 调度 |\\\\n\\\\n配套检查使用标准库 CPU 小模型和不变量，而不是目标设备实测：以有理数 sample 边界核对块几何；以显式窗口核对 DecodeReady 的 lookahead/startup 条件；用已知递增样本核对 overlap 裁剪和 sample offset；用离散到达轨迹核对 deadline 欠载；用独立公式核对首块时间、稳态占用和 PCM 字节。负对照包括漏掉 lookahead、只检查一个 codebook、重复发送左 overlap、忽略 deadline、用旧代次提交和把尾块补零当作稳态；这些故障必须由同一验证器拒绝，正确路径再被接受。检查不覆盖 GPU 内存可见性、真实 kernel 时间、声码器音质、WER 或服务使用效果。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-OMNI：Qwen2.5-Omni Technical Report](../sources/S-OMNI.md)：报告描述 Thinker/Talker 分支、块式模态输入、时间对齐和流式音频输出。§2.1、§2.3 与 §2.4 支持 Talker 接收高层表示和文本 embedding、产生语音 token，qwen-tts-tokenizer 的 causal audio decoder，Flow-Matching DiT 生成 mel，以及修改的 BigVGAN 生成波形；§2.4 还给出 sliding-window DiT 的 4 块窗口（2 个 lookback、当前块、1 个 lookahead）和首包延迟分解。本文据此推导块上下文、首包和播放时钟，不把报告架构推广为任意语音生成模型。\\\\n 的来源，不能据其 ASR 结果推出声码器或流式语音合成能力。\\\\n  [完整原文](../../references/S-MOONSHINE/reader.html) · [全文文本](../../references/S-MOONSHINE/fulltext.txt)\\\\n\\\\n- [S-WHISPER：Robust Speech Recognition via 怎样通过实现和实验区分竞争解释？\\\\n\\\\n这些是相关知识链的质量标准，不是每份文件必须照抄的六个标题。前置知识可以链接，但本章承担的核心算法、推导与边界不能用链接或名词清单代替。数学定义与真实硬件限制可以确定；某个引擎采用的分层、布局、算法和优化顺序应作为带前提的选择解释。\\\\n\\\\n## 正文与算法\\\\n\\\\n正文以问题和机制展开：说明问题为什么出现，定义对象和合法性，展开算法、数据流与状态更新，推导成本与组合关系，用设定算例、反例和区分实验解释结论如何改变。篇幅与结构由内容决定，不规定候选数、反例数或统一段落数量。\\\\n\\\\n实现逻辑可以转写为完整的算法伪代码，使用 pseudocode kernel、项目类结构、注册器、兼容分支和可执行命令保留在工程中。\\\\n\\\\n公式须说明符号、单位、轴和假设。区分逻辑数据量、实际设备事务量、容量峰值和关键路径时间；重叠工作不能把全部耗时直接相加。模型结构、数值策略、硬件能力或运行规模改变后，重新检查依赖与成本。\\\\n\\\\n## 来源阅读链\\\\n\\\\n论文保留直接可读的原始 PDF、必要图片和出处；来源说明用自己的话展开算法、推导、论文结论及其条件，明确哪些是论文报告、哪些是本库计算。文档同样保留原文，提炼定义、语义、约束及其设计含义。\\\\n\\\\n源码可以供知识编写者核对机制。交给 Agent 的内容应是经过核对的算法伪代码、数据流、状态关系与条件化事实，不能把整个实现文件称作知识原文。文档/源码混合资料按实际内容选择可读文档；文件扩展名、压缩包形式和仓库名称本身不决定知识价值。已有源码归档可以保留供溯源审计，其字节和哈希不因来源说明修订而改变。\\\\n\\\\n正文引用需要带实质内容，再指向来源说明；来源说明指向可读论文或文档。必要内容离线可读，不依赖 Agent 联网补全。准确版本留作证据身份；只有影响本题合法性或成本的版本事实进入论证，不搬运与本题无关的参数和分支。\\\\n\\\\n## 逐层阅读\\\\n\\\\n阅读入口按主题地图、章节摘要与问题/前提、二级节结构、完整论证、来源原文展开。Agent 自主选择阅读深度；索引与检索结果提供相邻机制，不产生必读清单。读取按实际字符范围与冻结修订记录；读过摘要不等于读过整章。\\\\n\\\\n## Base、观测和 workflow\\\\n\\\\nBase 的来源事实受发布版本的时间上限约束；编辑日期不改变事实日期。新的整理和独立推导保留真实日期与依据，后续实验不能伪装成历史 seed。\\\\n\\\\n运行观测保存环境、workload、测量方法、数值/单位/不确定性、实验证据与真实日期。机制知识解释因果、条件、预测和反例。Workflow 保存一类局部设计、诊断或验证问题的触发条件、前提、步骤、检查与退出/调整条件、成本和复用边界。三者相互引用，不能用一次成功代替机制解释或跨条件验证。\\\\n\\\\nEvolution 提炼、Diagnostician 独立复核，沿已有发布和证据机制进入后续冻结、检索与读取。Workflow 为可选方法，不自动成为 Controller 的全局顺序。跨任务资格使用现有权威晋升机制，负面与不确定结果保留，不建立平行资格体系。\\\\n\\\\n## 修订、覆盖和验证\\\\n\\\\n已有技术对象优先深化原章；独立对象才新增章节。修订保存登记前正文与元数据的准确字节，更新 catalog、来源说明哈希、导航、时间审计、VERSION 与变更清单。已存在的来源归档保持原身份。\\\\n\\\\n覆盖审计同时检查能力域、具体算法与跨机制组合，区分完整解释、仅提及、缺少推导、缺少证据和缺失；篇数和术语命中不是覆盖证明。结构/身份检查、独立算法算例、运行时读取/发布测试与真实构建效果分别报告。通过前几项不能声称已证明知识改善了 Agent 的系统设计或性能。\\\\n\\\\n六项标准的具体追问、组合案例、来源核对和使用效果边界见[知识内容审查](knowledge-review.md)。[Attention 模块](attention-module.md)是内容深度的已完成样例；其算法、硬件映射与组合状态按主题选择展开，不规定所有专题复制同样的结构。逐篇扩展状态见[扩展状态](expansion-status.json)，导航登记不代表深度验收完成。\\\\n\\\\n连续构建按[知识库构建 \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"required\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# 知识内容审查：从 Attention 样例推广\\\\n\\\\n本页把 Attention 多轮审查发现的问题整理为内容作者与审阅者可复用的问题。依据是[知识库构建方法](knowledge-method.md)中的六项标准，深度样例是[当前 Attention 模块](attention-module.md)。它不增加 Agent 的角色义务，也不要求每章采用同一结构、同样多的算例或统一的工程路线。\\\\n\\\\n## 知识库承担什么任务\\\\n\\\\n本库支持 InfraAgents 根据模型、workload、硬件和服务目标，从空工程构建、检验与持续优化完整推理系统。知识应提供五种帮助：还原问题的理论基础；区分合法条件与可探索的设计空间；给出足以独立实现的算法与状态关系；支持成本预测、实验和诊断；保存能够被反驳、修正和迁移的经验。\\\\n\\\\n一条有用的阅读链应支持读者形成这样的推理：任务与输入条件 → 正确性要求 → 候选算法与数据流 → 成本预测 → 区分实验 → 实现结果 → 修正后的结论。某一章可以承担其中一部分，但承担核心算法的地方不能只列注意事项或把关键步骤交给源码。\\\\n\\\\n## 六项标准怎样落实到实际问题\\\\n\\\\n| 内容标准 | 审阅时实际追问 | 过去发现的问题及其含义 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 原因、数学定义、输入输出和状态 | 为什么需要这个机制？每个量的轴、单位、范围和身份是什么？状态代表已知、已算、已确认还是已分配？ | FP8 只写“使用块尺度”不足以恢复分数和 PV 的共同单位；调度中的 token 已生成不等于其 KV 已计算 |\\\\n| 合法性与方案选择 | 哪条性质来自函数、数值契约或设备语义，哪条来自某个方案？等价性在实数、浮点还是特定误差范围内成立？ | 精确算术的归约结合性不能直接变成浮点逐位相同；图地址稳定不证明数据身份仍正确；内部 fragment 未公开就不能猜 lane 映射 |\\\\n| 算法、数据流和状态变化 | 能否写出初始化、推进、提交和结束？第一块、最后一块、空输入和失败分支怎样处理？每个被消费的量从哪里产生？ | 量化流程需要量化与恢复尺度；缓冲需要生产者、所有消费者及代次；硬件专题需要一条从逻辑 tile 到地址、线程、片上布局、指令输入和写回的完整路径 |\\\\n| 六类成本 | 是否在同一候选、相同输入和相同时间范围中列账？哪些量可以相加，哪些受关键路径和共享资源限制？ | 唯一 KV、各 head 请求流量和 DRAM 事务不能混算；共享容量只计一次；预留池与其中存活对象不能重复相加；深流水的驻留和 spill 会改变本来用于估时的吞吐 |\\\\n| 条件变化后的选择 | 改变 shape、状态组织、精度、到达轨迹或设备能力，哪条依赖保留，哪项成本改变？何种结果足以推翻原选择？ | 更多分区在并行度不足时有利，在已经饱和时可能只增加合并；更多缓冲不保证更快；缓存命中不保证新请求可立即执行 |\\\\n| 区分竞争解释 | 观察支持哪些解释？它们对某个可控改变给出什么不同预测？实验结果不符后怎样修改判断？ | “三级比两级慢”同时允许首尾、spill、驻留和未重叠解释；一次时间测量不能决定原因；软件事件模型不能证明 GPU 的内存可见性 |\\\\n\\\\n这些问题由主题决定使用范围。调度章节需要把就绪性、预算和输出归属连起来；缓存章节需要贯通身份、复制、发布和回收；硬件章节需要贯通布局、执行契约和资源。协议、统计或模型语义章节不必凭空增加矩阵指令实例。\\\\n\\\\n## 从单个机制走到组合案例\\\\n\\\\n分开解释各个机制之后，选择会改变合法性或成本的真实交界，追踪一次完整变化。例如共享前缀和私有尾块在追加、封存、发布、消费与回收期间，内容、scale、页表和读者必须属于一致的状态；调度器选中的工作必须已有上游输入和容量，而执行视图的压紧不能改变请求归属。\\\\n\\\\n审阅者沿一次轨迹检查：发生了什么输入事件；哪些对象仍存活；谁能写；谁已经取得读取权；何时对消费者可见；失败后哪些旧状态仍有效；取消后哪些工作仍在途；何时能把同一物理资源交给下一使用者。对象需要身份或代次时，解释防止的具体错误。只有单次同步执行的算法不必引入多代次协议。\\\\n\\\\n交界还包括“看似已经完成，下一步却没有输入”的状态。本轮调度审阅发现：完整命中 KV 而没有末行 logits 时，只按已知长度减 KV 长度选择工作会得到零，无法生成第一个新 token。修订明确了安全重算最后一个已知 token 的路径及共享写区隔离。沿状态图检查是否存在有合法请求却无后继事件的停滞，比只检查各状态的字段范围更有用。\\\\n\\\\n组合案例应使读者能计算至少一项会影响决定的代价，并解释另一种选择何时反转。重点是让独立机制能够正确拼接，不是枚举所有组合。示例的页长、tile、队列策略和版本字段均为可替换选择。\\\\n\\\\n## 阅读链与事实核对\\\\n\\\\n先检查正文承担的核心知识，再检查直接来源说明与足以支持关键事实的固定论文或文档。保留原始资料的错误、版本身份和字节，在解释中纠正公式或限定结论；自己的推导不能归为论文实测。源码可以用于作者核对，但读者独立实现所需的事实应进入允许读取的算法说明。\\\\n\\\\n审查记录写明读过哪些正文、哪些来源及其范围、发现的具体问题、实际修改与检查。只有读取摘要、术语检索或运行链接检查的专题，继续保留深度复核待完成状态。没有必要为了一个确定问题递归阅读所有引用。\\\\n\\\\n## 内容与使用效果分别验收\\\\n\\\\n内容审查判断六项标准在声明范围内是否有充分解释。作者侧算例验证代数、布局、边界、协议或成本模型；它需要独立参考、不变量或能触发错误的负对照，不能只让测试复述实现。读取测试检查冻结内容能否被取回及身份是否匹配。这三类证据各自有效，不能互相代替。\\\\n\\\\n直接使用检验让 Agent 在没有现成实现的情况下处理正文未直接演示的问题：重新推导合法算法，改变输入或硬件条件后重算，面对错误提出竞争解释，收到反证后修改方案。保存允许资料、任务、模型/上下文、预算、答卷或实现、执行结果及失败归因。交叉审阅兼做推导练习可以发现内容缺口，但有共同上下文、作者经验或未隔离的环境时，只能声称完成这次练习。\\\\n\\\\n如果要声称“知识改善了 Agent 的构建能力”，还需可比的知识版本或对照条件、多个代表任务以及预先说明的判断方法。目标 GPU 的数值、同步、重叠和性能仍需设备结果。没有最佳 tile 或流水级数不构成知识缺陷；没有解释如何推导候选、识别限制、测量与修正，才是内容缺口。\\\\n\\\\n## 怎样给出审查结论\\\\n\\\\n对每个问题给出正文位置、明确结论与证据边界，区分“已完整解释”“仅提及”“缺推导”“缺证据”“缺失”。这些描述可按实际内容组合使用，不转成总分或用测试数量抵消关键算法缺口。\\\\n\\\\n已经修复的问题在新修订中复核后关闭，不沿用旧审查中“仍缺 FP8/硬件映射/组合案例”的判断。新的缺口必须来自当前字节。Attention 当前的两个具体案例已补足内容展开，实际 Agent 独立构建与目标 GPU 效果仍有各自的验证边界。以当前内容和当前证据决定结论，不为了持续审查而不断增加验收条件。\\\\n\\\\n扩展工作优先完成相关专题的一条知识链，再复核跨专题衔接。当前批次与逐篇状态见[扩展状态](expansion-status.json)；历史审查保留当时结论，不覆盖成当前状态。\\\\n\\\", \\\"9cab040f27f77dc8040a6cc6f0ae96a175542e4379e2262ca2cdb53fb9aee3a4\\\", \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"required\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-MODEL-011：语音生成：Codec Token、声学块与播放时钟\\\\n\\\\n语音服务需要把模型生成时钟转换为音频播放时钟，首包和稳定供给由多个阶段共同决定。\\\\n\\\\n## 常见生成链的状态\\\\n\\\\n文本或语义条件驱动声学 token 生成，codec/vocoder 将其变成波形。不同模型可能使用自回归 codec、并行多个 codebook、扩散或 flow 解码。一个声学 token 不一定对应一个固定文本 token，也不一定能立即独立解码成可播放样本。\\\\n\\\\ncodec 的帧率、codebook 数、采样率和 chunk overlap 定义输出几何。例如声学帧率 50 Hz 时，10 帧代表 200 ms 音频；模型生成它们花费 40 ms，局部生成实时率为 0.2，但首包还要等待足够的声学上下文和 vocoder 处理。这个算例解释吞吐充裕仍可能首包很慢。\\\\n\\\\n## 流式解码的边界\\\\n\\\\n若 vocoder 需要右侧 lookahead，最前面一段样本只有拿到未来若干帧后才稳定。相邻 chunk 可能保留重叠用于衔接，发给客户端时必须裁去重复部分并维持累计样本位置。不能把网络 chunk 数当声学帧数，也不能在 EOS 前后任意补静音而不改变任务。\\\\n\\\\n自回归声学分支的 KV、codec 状态、波形 overlap 与文本对齐进度组成请求状态。取消应停止后续生成并释放这些对象，但在途 audio chunk 仍可能已经送入播放队列。用户“停止说话”的体验因此还受客户端缓冲长度影响。\\\\n\\\\n## 用缓冲模型推导服务目标\\\\n\\\\n设客户端缓冲中尚未播放音频时长为 B(t)，网络可播放音频到达速率为 a(t)，正常播放消耗速率为 1，则缓冲变化近似 dB/dt＝a(t)−1。平均 a＞1 不排除瞬时断供；B 太小易卡顿，太大增加可感知延迟和取消迟滞。\\\\n\\\\n服务目标可同时约束首段音频时间、实时率、缓冲欠载频率和最终质量。减少 chunk 大小降低初始等待，却增加调度、封包和 vocoder 边界成本。不同语言、语速与停顿分布会改变声学输出长度，负载模型应直接统计音频时长和块分布。\\\\n\\\\n## 各种生成链需要各自的执行预算\\\\n\\\\n自回归声学 token、codec token 到 mel 的迭代 flow/扩散、mel 到 waveform 的 vocoder，分别消耗不同的状态、矩阵工作和窗口。直接因果 codec 解码、一次生成完整声学表示、以及分块迭代解码不能用同一个“每 token 耗时”比较。多 codebook 的生成顺序和延迟排列也决定何时凑齐一个可解码声学帧。\\\\n\\\\nQwen2.5-Omni 固定报告的具体路径是 Talker 生成语音 token，Flow-Matching DiT 生成 mel，再经修改的 BigVGAN 产生 waveform；DiT block 可见范围为当前块加两块 lookback 和一块 lookahead。需要未来 code block 不等于必须等待相同长度的墙钟时间：如果 code 生成快于实时，可以提前生成所需未来块，代价表现为额外模型步骤、状态和首次启动工作。\\\\n\\\\n跨请求聚批可以分别发生在 Talker、flow step 和 vocoder，条件是 shape、所处求解阶段和上下文合法。为了合成大 batch 等待太久，会先耗尽客户端播放缓冲。调度按下一块最迟可播放时间与缺口安排工作，比只最大化整段音频/秒更贴合流式目标；不具备中途抢占能力的长 kernel 还会形成不可绕过的阻塞。\\\\n\\\\n## 一个声学块的首包与稳态算例\\\\n\\\\n以下为通用服务设定，不声称某个已发表模型的 codec 帧率。声学帧率 50 Hz，每块 10 帧对应 200 ms 音频，需要一块 lookahead；code 生成速度设为 500 帧/s，flow/vocoder 合计每块 25 ms，封包发送 5 ms，且文本条件已就绪。首块需 20 帧 code，共 40 ms，再解码和发送，首包为 70 ms。稳态每块只新增 10 帧，可串行用 20+25+5=50 ms 供给 200 ms 音频，对应这条设定路径的实时率 0.25。\\\\n\\\\n若文本或语义条件还需等待 150 ms，首音频即变为 220 ms；若 flow 阶段与其他请求竞争产生 180 ms 排队，良好的平均实时率仍不能保证不断音。减少为 5 帧块可能降低首次 code 等待，却增大解码/封包调用次数和边界开销。完整声学表示一次解码可提高大批效率，但首包要等整段条件/声学生成；是否允许这种等待由任务决定。\\\\n\\\\n24 kHz、单声道、16-bit PCM 的 200 ms 块有 4800 个样本、9600 字节；400 ms 客户端缓冲含 19200 字节。编码压缩可降低网络 bytes，却不取消声音所代表的播放时间。测客户端可播放块的到达时间和连续 sample offset，不能用服务器 token 完成时间代替声音实际开始。\\\\n\\\\n## 打断、抖动与质量一起测\\\\n\\\\n打断时使旧响应代次不再接收新块，取消未提交模型工作，并让在途 compute、传输、codec 状态和 overlap 安全结束。客户端也要丢弃尚未播放的旧代次数据；仅服务端停生成，已缓冲音频仍会继续播放。已播放样本无法撤销，协议要明确最后确认的 sample offset 和新响应从何处开始。\\\\n\\\\n联合实验固定文本/语义输入与音色条件，扫描 chunk、lookahead、并发、突发、慢客户端和网络抖动。报告首可播放样本、平均与尾部实时率、缓冲欠载时长、打断到静音、最终音频时长、内容一致性和自然度。ASR 回转的 WER 只覆盖可懂内容的一部分，不能代替音色、韵律、接缝和噪声验证；裁去失败块、补静音或改变语速必须作为输出语义变化披露。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance 已完成。flush 先让重采样器与特征窗按模型契约处理残留，再让 encoder 处理最后未提交位置和所需右上下文，最后完成源投影与发布。尾部不足 lookahead 时，只能采用模型明确允许的 padding、边界 mask 或末块规则；没有允许路径则返回 FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT。填充值不算真实采样，提交偏移不超过实际收到的源末端。flush 也可能耗尽时间片，应保存其阶段和残留后继续，而非提前发布完成。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nALGORITHM ConsumeKnownInput(req, src)\\\\n前提：i=req.n < length(req.known)，src 为合法 READY 产物\\\\n输出：位置 i 的各层 KV、末层 logits，或失败\\\\n1. i ← req.n；h ← 模型规定的 Embed(req.known[i]) 与位置 i 的组合；\\\\n2. 为本次位置建立未提交的逐层写入区；\\\\n3. 对 decoder 层 l 从低到高：\\\\n       q, k, v ← 从 h 做 self 投影并应用规定的位置变换；\\\\n       在第 l 层位置 i 暂写 k, v；不得重新追加位置 0..i−1；\\\\n       a ← 对历史 0..i 和当前 k/v 做合法 self attention；\\\\n       x ← 按模型顺序处理 self 输出投影、残差、norm；\\\\n       若该层有 cross：\\\\n           检查 M_{l,i} 非空且已就绪；\\\\n           c ← 用 x 的 query 与该模块 src.K/V 做 cross attention；\\\\n           r ← 按模型顺序处理 cross 输出投影、残差、norm；\\\\n       否则 r ← x；\\\\n       h ← 按模型定义执行 FFN、残差、norm，作为下一层输入；\\\\n4. logits ← OutputHead(末端处理(h))；\\\\n5. 全部层成功后，原子提交位置 i，req.n ← i＋1；\\\\n6. 若 req.n＝length(req.known)：保存 logits，标记其预测位置为 req.n；\\\\n   否则丢弃此中间位置的生成 logits，继续消费已知 prompt/强制前缀；\\\\n7. 失败时不推进 n；撤销暂写或标记请求失败，不暴露部分层长度。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n实际实现可以一次处理多个未计算的 prompt 位置，但各层 attention mask 必须同时覆盖历史与新增位置，新增位置内部仍因果。上述逐位置写法用来明确数据依赖，并非要求每个位置单独启动 kernel。\\\\n\\\\n初始化要求 m≥1、n＝0、known＝P、各层 self KV 为空、待选 logits 为空、生成计数 g＝0。max_new_tokens 只计生成 token，不计任务前缀；是否将 EOS 计入 usage 按协议规定，本文 g 将它作为一个已选择的生成 token 计入。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nALGORITHM RunDecoderSlice(req, src, execution_budget)\\\\n输入：已初始化或可恢复的请求、源产物、调度时间片\\\\n输出：可恢复暂停、等待事件、带原因的终态或失败\\\\n1. 若取消或代次过期：停止未来提交，返回 CANCELLED；\\\\n2. 若源依赖不兼容：返回 NEED_REBUILD；按源更新规则重建后才能继续；\\\\n3. 重复：\\\\n   a. 若已有失败：保存原因并返回 FAILED；\\\\n   b. 若源尾部契约已被判为不可满足：返回 FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT；\\\\n   c. 若 g 已到 max_new_tokens 且尚无目标停止原因：设置 TARGET_LENGTH；\\\\n   d. 若已有合法目标停止原因：\\\\n          若源 flush 未完成：返回 WAIT_SOURCE_FINAL；\\\\n          若停止依据仍适用于最终源且尾部已处理：\\\\n              提交允许的最终后缀，发布 END_OF_REQUEST(目标停止原因)；\\\\n              返回；\\\\n          否则返回 NEED_REBUILD；\\\\n   e. 若当前操作缺少合法源视图或所需 lookahead：返回 WAIT_MORE_SOURCE；\\\\n   f. 若时间片已耗尽：保存进度，返回 PAUSED_BUDGET；\\\\n   g. 若 n < length(known)：\\\\n          ConsumeKnownInput(req, src)；计入本片工作；继续循环；\\\\n   h. 要求 n＝length(known)，且保存的 logits 预测位置为 n；\\\\n      若没有该 logits：返回 FAILED_MISSING_LOGITS；\\\\n   i. 按任务约束从 logits 选择下一个 token y；\\\\n      原子保存选择结果、随机状态与任务约束状态；\\\\n      将 y 追加到 known 和暂定输出；g ← g＋1；清除待选 logits；\\\\n      若 y 为合法 EOS：设置 TARGET_EOS；\\\\n      否则若 g＝max_new_tokens：设置 TARGET_LENGTH；\\\\n      按稳定规则检查可以提交的文本及源样本边界；计入本片工作；\\\\n      继续循环。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n消费输入和选择输出是两个可恢复步骤。在最后一个 prompt 消费后暂停，恢复时先选择 y_0；在选择 y_0 后暂停，恢复时只消\\\\n\\\\n[EXCERPT extracted-character range 8000:13899]\\\\n00 条已编码请求的 cross 合计为 4.57763671875 GiB，只保存 E 为 195.3125 MiB。另设 L_self＝12、D_self＝1024、n＝100、每元素 2 字节，则每请求 self＝4,915,200 字节＝4.6875 MiB。这是同宽配置算例，不表示 self、cross 和 encoder 必须同宽同层数。\\\\n\\\\n计算以一次乘加记一个 MAC。逐行 dense cross 源投影约需 S Σ_c d_e(D_Kc＋D_Vc) MAC；固定源重复使用 R 次时，逐次重投影支付 R 倍，缓存只支付一次。目标 query 投影、attention 和 FFN 仍需执行。\\\\n\\\\n对单个模块，设 query head 数为 H_q，key 维度 d_k，value 维度 d_v，可见 key 数为 N。每个新增 query 的 QK 与 PV 合计约为 H_q N(d_k＋d_v) MAC，softmax 另有 O(H_q N) 标量工作。GQA/MQA 按 H_kv 存储，但 query 侧运算仍按 H_q 组织；减少 KV heads 不自动按同比例减少 attention 算术。\\\\n\\\\n若固定 prompt 长度为 m，新增消费 G 个位置、完整目标历史都可见，则每层 self 的 QK/PV 项为 Θ((mG＋G²)H_q d_h)，这里假设 d_k＝d_v＝d_h。固定源的 cross 项为 Θ(GS H_q,cross d_h,cross)。这些是各模块 attention 项，不是完整 decoder 成本：self/cross 的 query 投影、self 新 K/V 投影、输出投影、FFN、归一化、输出词表头和采样均另计。prompt prefill 本身也有工作，不能只计后续 G 步。\\\\n\\\\nencoder 的 dense 双向 attention 每层有 O(S²H_q d_h) 项，FFN 和投影另计；若物理执行包含 padding，应以实际计算长度而非 S_valid 估算。变长 encoder 可减少短源的无效计算，但不能据此推断质量或任意分块能力。\\\\n\\\\n逻辑读取上，每个 decoder query 需要访问其可见 cross K/V；如果每步都从 HBM 取回完整缓存，R 步流量约为 R 倍 cross 字节。该式是所设读取路径，真实 DRAM 事务还受片上复用、head 共享、batch、布局和重复加载影响。主存换入 GPU 时，还要计主存读取、链路传输、设备写入及后续设备读取，不能只用缓存容量代替全路径流量。\\\\n\\\\nencoder/decoder 分设备时，可传 E 后在 decoder 侧投影，也可在源侧投影后传全部 cross K/V。上述算例后者主体字节是前者的 24 倍；是否值得仍取决于投影算力、链路、复用次数和重叠。同步发布后消费者才能读取，未完成传输不能作为有效缓存。\\\\n\\\\n准备成本包括重采样、特征窗历史、tokenization、任务前缀和时间戳映射。同步包括源就绪、投影发布、目标位置事务和稳定结果提交。驻留包括原始缓冲、特征、encoder 状态、E、cross/self KV、暂定输出与在途副本；共享物理页只计一次，但每个读者生命周期独立。阶段队列有界才能限制 encoder 领先造成的源产物积压。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化怎样改变方案\\\\n\\\\n固定源、较长目标通常增加缓存投影的价值；短目标可能不足以摊薄构建与管理开销。只存 E、提前投影全部 cross、decoder 准入后投影、按层重投影或换入，是不同的计算、流量与驻留选择。先计算投影节省，再检查它是否被缓存读取、迁移或并发下降抵消。\\\\n\\\\n源每次更新都改变旧表示时，应放弃精确追加缓存；必要时重建 cross 和目标状态。原生稳定源前缀只解决源投影追加问题，不自动证明目标 self 状态可按完整新源语义继续。更换精度、位置规则或 backend 后，重新检查数值和布局身份。\\\\n\\\\n更小源块减少采集等待，却增加调用、边界处理和不稳定输出；更大块减少启动次数，却增加首段等待。lookahead 是模型契约和质量条件，不是可任意删减的性能参数。重采样与特征窗跨包延续，不能每个网络包重新初始化。\\\\n\\\\nWhisper 固定论文描述 16 kHz 音频、80 通道 log-magnitude Mel、25 ms 窗、10 ms 步长和 30 秒音频块；任务、语言及时间戳规则通过 decoder token 表达，时间戳相对当前窗口并以 20 ms 量化。长音频 buffered transcription 根据预测时间戳推进窗口，并可使用前文条件。这条路径需要恢复全局时间和处理跨窗口词，不证明 cross KV 可随任意新包追加。\\\\n\\\\nMoonshine 的固定论文版本采用变长音频和 strides 为 64、3、2 的卷积 stem，以 RoPE 表达位置。论文报告短输入可减少固定 padding 工作，同时指出极短音频的重复输出及超过训练长度的质量限制；其中训练样本组装规则采用约 4 到 30 秒区间。变长输入、反复识别已采集窗口、按稳定块持续推进是不同能力，不能由名称相互推出。\\\\n\\\\n## 场景：八路低延迟转写\\\\n\\\\n以下全部为设计设定。八条会话输入 16 kHz、单声道、16-bit PCM，每条每 200 ms 产生 3200 个样本、6400 字节，总输入为 256000 字节/s。目标是在任务允许的稳定规则下，首个稳定片段距首个相关采样不超过 500 ms，并满足固定评测集上的质量门槛。\\\\n\\\\nA 等完整 1 秒窗口再识别；B 每 200 ms 重跑增长窗口并允许修订；C 使用明确支持 200 ms 提交块、100 ms lookahead 的模型。A 的采集等待已超过目标。B 可早给暂定文字，却支付重复编码且不能把首次猜测当稳定提交。C 的合法性依赖模型与 processor，不能直接赋予 Whisper 或 Moonshine。\\\\n\\\\n设 C 的排队/聚批为 25 ms、encoder 40 ms、decoder 35 ms、发布 10 ms，且这条首块路径依次发生，则 200＋100＋25＋40＋35＋10＝410 ms。八路每秒共 40 块，每块在同一串行资源占用 75 ms，则资源需求为 3 秒/s，队列无法长期稳定。若八块合批后整组执行 110 ms，每 200 ms 服务一组的该资源占用为 55%；实际相位、聚批等待、质量和长尾仍待测量。可重叠阶段应按依赖与共享资源重新计算，不能无条件相加或取最大值。\\\\n\\\\n一条组合轨迹是：采集区间及 lookahead 到齐，processor 延续历史并生成特征；encoder 发布合法源版本；cross 投影完成后 decoder 获得读取权；消费任务前缀末位置，保存预测 y_0 的 logits；时间片结束，状态进入 PAUSED_BUDGET；下一次调度在同一源上选择 y_0，再消费它，逐层追加 KV；稳定规则满足后提交文本与全局样本偏移。最后收到结束包时，先完成尾部处理；目标若未结束则继续调度，直到合法 EOS 或明确长度终止后才发布请求终态。\\\\n\\\\n若新源改变旧表示，重建发生在旧目标状态继续使用之前。若途中取消，停止发布，旧代次在途结果不得写入新请求；其缓冲仍等最后使用者结束。慢客户端会延长目标状态驻留，应通过输出额度反向限制生成，而非无界领先。\\\\n\\\\n验证固定相同原始音频、标注与文字标准化，计算 WER＝(替换＋删除＋插入)/参考词数；适用语言另定义 CER。静音、极短指令、噪声、跨块词、长句和慢客户端共同覆盖边界，记录暂定修订、稳定延迟、最终质量、失败、队列和实时率。处理耗时/音频时长小于 1 只是平均实时率条件，不能证明首段稳定延迟达标。只要求整段最终结果时 A 可能更合算；允许修订且重复计算可承受时 B 有价值；稳定延迟严格时再验证 C 的模型与服务联合条件。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断与可反驳检查\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 区分实验与修正方向 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| prompt 后没有输出 | 末行 logits 丢失、未选择首 token、错误等待源 | 固定已就绪源，在最后 prompt 消费后暂停再恢复；要求先选择 y_0，缓存长度仍为 m |\\\\n| 恢复后文本重复或 KV 过长 | 完整前缀重复追加、同一 logits 重采样 | 比较连续执行与不同时间片切分的消费位置、选择次数、随机状态和最终输出 |\\\\n| 最后源包到达后过早完成 | 把源结束或预算耗尽当目标终止 | 在最后源已 flush、目标尚未 EOS 时耗尽预算；应暂停并能在同一源继续 |\\\\n| 新版本输出出现旧内容 | cross 复用错误、上层 self KV/logits 仍依赖旧源 | 分别重建 cross 与完整目标状态；只有后者恢复一致时，修正目标依赖判断 |\\\\n| 缓存减少投影但总时延不降 | 带宽、驻留下降、排队或传输主导 | 固定输入比较投影时间、流量、在途字节和队列；计算项下降不能单独支持整体收益 |\\\\n| 边界 WER 变差 | 上下文不足、时间戳映射或拼接错误 | 分别改变 lookahead 和全局拼接；单窗正确而全局错误优先检查提交映射 |\\\\n\\\\n随章检查使用标准库 CPU 小模型：以非对称矩阵的字面投影结果和多源非均匀 softmax 解析式核对算术；保留旧 K/V、仅投影新增行并与完整重算比较；用独立的完整前缀计算路径核对简化两层 decoder 的增量状态；比较连续执行与时间片暂停恢复。它还分别检查原始空、特征全无效、encoder 输出全无效，以及跨兼容版本的提交单调性。\\\\n\\\\n负对照包括错误 causal-cross、未来目标可见、修改源后沿用旧缓存、把已选择 token 提前计为已计算、旧 ledger 放行新版本偏移回退、空检查后置和预算耗尽后直接结束。故障产生的状态或事件必须送入与正常路径相同的不变量判定器并被拒绝，不能仅打印“故障函数返回了错误值”。\\\\n\\\\n这些检查覆盖小模型算术、缓存数据流和调度状态关系。真实模型的位置/norm/量化实现、GPU 内存可见性、kernel、WER、负载时延和知识使用效果均需独立证据；本章没有报告相应实测。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-TRANSFORMER：Attention Is All You Need](../sources/S-TRANSFORMER.md)：Transformer 上限约束，编辑日期不作为事实发布日期。来源论文的设备与质量结果不等于本库设备实验；本文 CPU 检查也不证明真实模型或服务性能。\\\\n\\\\n## 延伸阅读\\\\n\\\\n- [交叉注意力缓存：固定源、独立几何与可见性](../algorithms/cross-attention-cache.md)。\\\\n- [语音生成：Codec \\\"knowledge/workloads/metric-events.md\\\", \\\"sha256\\\": \\\"c21db7895f35f10ebe16fe4fc795de05ea48de02cd90339712f9a4a49252d1bb\\\", \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-WORK-001：服务指标：事件边界、Token 间隔与用户时间\\\\n\\\\n一个延迟指标是两个明确事件的时间差；指标名字相同而事件定义不同，会导致不同结论。\\\\n\\\\n## 一条生成请求的时间轴\\\\n\\\\n记客户端发送为 t₀，服务接收为 tᵣ，首个内容 token 可见为 t₁，最后内容为 tₙ，协议完成为 t𝒻。客户端 TTFT＝t₁−t₀ 包含网络、排队、预处理和首步执行；服务内部的首 token latency 若从 tᵣ 或开始执行计时，则是另一指标。结束延迟通常与 t𝒻−t₀ 有关，可能包含最后封包和传输。\\\\n\\\\n对 N>1 个输出 token，平均 TPOT 常定义为 (tₙ−t₁)/(N−1)；N＝1 时没有 token 间隔，应单独处理。逐 token ITL 是相邻内容 token 的时间差，p99 ITL 反映间歇停顿，不能由平均 TPOT 推断。若传输 chunk 包含多 token，客户端只能直接观测 chunk 时间，逐 token 时间需要额外定义。\\\\n\\\\n## 聚合顺序改变含义\\\\n\\\\n先算每请求平均 TPOT 再平均，给每请求相同权重；把所有 token 间隔合并后平均，长输出权重大。先求每请求 p99 再平均，不等于所有间隔的全局 p99。吞吐的分母应说明是完整测量窗口、从首发到末完成，还是只计算稳定区间。\\\\n\\\\n空角色事件、心跳和 usage 消息不能自动计为首个内容。detokenization 缓冲和 stop string 检测可能让模型已产生 token 而用户尚未收到字符，这个延迟属于真实服务体验。\\\\n\\\\n## 非文本输出的事件\\\\n\\\\n语音关注首个可播放包、累计音频时长和供给间隙；视频/图像关注完整可用输出或明确的预览事件。一个音频包对应多长播放时间比“多少 tokens/s”更直接。多模态服务可以同时报告文本和音频两条时间线，并使用各自 SLO。\\\\n\\\\n将模型计算事件与客户端消费事件连接起来，才能解释优化究竟减少了哪一段时间。内部 kernel 加速若被协议缓冲掩盖，用户 TTFT 可以保持不变。\\\\n\\\\n## 为不同任务选择完成事件\\\\n\\\\n| 任务 | 可交付结果的事件 | 需要同时保留的条件 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 多轮会话或工具流程 | 必要依赖完成且最终回答可用 | 中间回合、工具失败、取消和会话级质量 |\\\\n| Embedding | 全部规定向量已返回且可供消费 | 输入条数、维度、归一化与数值/检索质量 |\\\\n| 检索与 reranking | 满足过滤规则的排序结果可用 | top-k、候选集、索引版本和 recall/排序质量 |\\\\n| 图像生成或识别 | 完整图像或规定预测结果可用 | 分辨率、预处理、生成步数及质量条件 |\\\\n| 语音识别 | 首个稳定文本与最终转录分别可用 | 音频窗口、修订规则和词错误率等目标 |\\\\n| 语音/视频生成 | 可连续消费的包及完整输出 | 播放时长、间隙、帧顺序与联合质量 |\\\\n\\\\n生成 tokens/s 不能替代这些任务的完成率。会话有 5 次模型调用时，5 个请求成功不一定意味着整个工具流程成功；embedding 的长文档分块数量增加也不能直接算作业务吞吐增加。度量单位要与用户需要的产物一致。\\\\n\\\\n## 时钟、边界与未完成样本\\\\n\\\\n同一进程的时间差应使用适合测量持续时间的时钟；跨机器事件相减还需要已知的时钟同步误差。trace 身份可以连接因果关系，但不能自动使时钟精确对齐。对很短的网络/设备阶段，测量误差可能与所报告变化同量级。\\\\n\\\\n测量窗口内到达但尚未完成的请求不能消失。可以采用固定到达窗口后排空并报告总完成情况，也可以报告稳定窗口的吞吐并单列窗口边界与残留队列；两者的分母不同。超时、拒绝、取消与质量不合格分别标记，按目标定义进入成功率和延迟解释。\\\\n\\\\n## 成本与能量的分母\\\\n\\\\n单位有效输出成本=所选时间与资源边界内的总成本/有效输出数，单位有效输出能量同理。分子包含失败、缓存预热、空闲保留和重算所消耗的资源。整机能量与仅设备能量需分开；为保持比较可解释，说明是否扣除空闲基线，以及为何该口径符合使用目标。\\\\n\\\\n若新方案返回更少 token、更低分辨率或更短音频，吞吐与能效改善可能来自任务改变。应先核对任务与质量，再将同一有效输出单位的延迟、成本和能量一起比较。相关的尾部样本与区间条件见 [实验统计](../tools/statistical-experiments.md)。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-GENAI-PERF：NVIDIA GenAI-Perf](../sources/S-GENAI-PERF.md)：GenAI-Perf 的指标围绕请求、响应、首个内容、流式间隔、输出长度和测量窗口定义。客户端 chunk 与模型 token 并非必然一一对应。\\\\n  [完整原文](../../references/S-GENAI-PERF/reader.html) · [全文文本](../../references/S-GENAI-PERF/fulltext.txt)\\\\n\\\\n- [S-MLPERF-LLM：MLPerf Inference — Llama 2 与 LoadGen（固定历史版本）](../sources/S-MLPERF-LLM.md)：MLPerf 的 Llama 2 服务基准将特定任务、到达模型、质量和延迟条件组织成评测协议，服务能力依赖这些共同条件。\\\\n  [算法与机制说明](../sources/S-MLPERF-LLM.md)\\\\n\\\\n- [S-ASGI：ASGI — HTTP and WebSocket Message Format](../sources/S-ASGI.md)：ASGI HTTP/WebSocket 规范定义接收、发送、响应体和断开相关事件；断开通知与发送失败可能存在时间上的竞争。\\\\n  [完整原文](../../references/S-ASGI/reader.html) · [全文文本](../../references/S-ASGI/fulltext.txt)\\\\n\\\\n正文中的公式展开、容量算例与组合设计是基于这些来源的推导；设定算例不冒充实测。来源版本受 Token、声学块与播放时钟](../models/speech-generation.md)。\\\\n- [主机与设备时间：偏序、区间并集和关键路径](../system-semantics/host-device-timing.md)。\\\\n\\\", \\\"excerpt_ranges\\\": [[0, 2891]], \\\"range_unit\\\":
